schema.label: Design
schema.text: This is an international multi-centre, open-label, randomized phase III trial in participants with metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) comparing: 1) systemic therapy at the investigator’s discretion and no SBRT; 2) the addition of stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to extra -cranial oligoprogressive disease and continuation of first -line systemic therapy with standard of care (SOC) immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) +/- chemotherapy.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: First-line systemic therapy (ICI alone versus ICI and chemotherapy) Number of oligoprogressive lesions (1, 2 versus 3, 4 or 5) Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (0, 1 versus 2)

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Participants with metastatic NSCLC on first-line ICI- based systemic therapy having received at least 3 cycles Restaging studies reveal ≤ 5 extracranial oligoprogressive lesions, all of which must be amenable to SBRT* Oligoprogressive lesions are asymptomatic, not requiring palliative radiotherapy at the time of study enrollment

schema.label: Randomize

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Systemic therapy at the investigator’s discretion, no SBRT Continue with SOC treatment until disease progression** Follow-up for survival (every 12 weeks)

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: SBRT/radiotherapy* to all sites of oligoprogression followed by the same first-line SOC systemic therapy permitted. Please see Section 7.0 for further details.

schema.note: N = 320 participants If a metastatic site is best treated with hypofractionated radiation instead of SBRT, this will be See Section 8.0 for guidelines regarding disease progression.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: REPEAT is a multicenter single-arm phase II trial of preoperative partial-breast reirradiation and repeat breast-conserving surgery for an ipsilateral breast recurrence after prior breast-conserving therapy. Planned enrolment is 25.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Age 50 or older, unifocal non-lobular invasive carcinoma 2 cm or smaller, Bloom-Richardson grade 1 or 2, estrogen-receptor positive, HER2 negative, and clinically node negative.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: There is no randomization. All patients receive one radiotherapy and surgery sequence.

arms.label: Preoperative PBI then surgery
arms.text: Single-fraction partial-breast irradiation, 20 Gy to the tumor and 15 Gy to the surrounding 2 cm of breast, on a conventional or MR-guided linac, using CT and MRI in the treatment position. Breast-conserving surgery follows at 3 weeks, plus or minus 1 week.

NCT06640881.schema_source: Open-access BMJ Open protocol (PMC12273098); the single-arm dose and eligibility are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Retro-Ion is a single-center randomized phase II pilot of neoadjuvant particle radiotherapy for resectable or marginally resectable retroperitoneal soft-tissue sarcoma.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized to protons or carbon ions. Both arms use active scanning and the same prescription.

arms.label: Protons
arms.text: Neoadjuvant protons, 39 Gy (RBE) in 13 fractions, 5 to 6 fractions per week, then surgery.

arms.label: Carbon ions
arms.text: Neoadjuvant carbon ions, 39 Gy (RBE) in 13 fractions, 5 to 6 fractions per week, then surgery.

NCT04219202.schema_source: Open-access Trials protocol (PMC7881463); both arm doses are stated in the methods.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SABR-ROC is a multicenter phase III trial of standard care with or without SABR for recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer after primary treatment. Target enrolment is 270. Eligible patients have 10 or fewer metastases, each 5 cm or smaller.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Stratification uses three factors: how many of platinum sensitivity, absent ascites, normal CA-125, and ECOG 0-1 are present (0-3 versus 4); recurrence with versus without lymph nodes; and PARP-inhibitor use versus non-use.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Randomization is 1:2.

arms.label: Arm 1 standard care
arms.text: Standard systemic care chosen from guidelines and multidisciplinary discussion.

arms.label: Arm 2 standard care plus SABR
arms.text: The same standard care plus SABR to recurrent lesions seen on imaging. Fraction number may be 1 to 10, and the accepted dose range is 16-45 Gy.

NCT05444270.schema_source: Open-access BMC Cancer protocol (PMC10588104); arms, ratio, and stratification are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SABR-SYNC is a phase III trial for oligometastatic cancer with a synchronous primary and up to 10 metastases. Planned enrolment is 180. Overall survival is the primary endpoint.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified by histology and by the number of metastases at enrolment.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Randomization is 1:2 between palliative-intent standard care and standard care plus ablative treatment to all known disease. Surgery, thermal ablation, or conventional radiation may replace SABR when clinically preferred.

arms.label: Standard care
arms.text: Palliative-intent standard-of-care treatment.

arms.label: Standard care plus SABR
arms.text: Standard care plus ablative therapy, preferably SABR, to the primary and all metastases. Recommended SABR regimens are 20 Gy in 1 fraction, 30 Gy in 3 fractions, or 35 Gy in 5 fractions.

NCT05717166.schema_source: Open-access BMC Palliative Care protocol (PMC11380777); the 1:2 randomization and recommended doses are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SAHARA is a multicenter open-label randomized phase II non-inferiority trial of radiotherapy with or without mild water-filtered infrared-A hyperthermia for invasive non-melanoma skin cancer. Planned enrolment is 100.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Histologically confirmed invasive basal or squamous cell carcinoma, stage T2 or higher, age 65 or older, and ECOG 0-2. Local recurrence is allowed if prior non-radiotherapy treatment was more than 6 months earlier.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Two arms compare 2-year local control, defined as no need for further intervention.

arms.label: Hyperthermia plus de-escalated RT
arms.text: Mild water-filtered infrared-A hyperthermia immediately followed by 5 Gy x 6 fractions over 3 weeks.

arms.label: Standard RT
arms.text: 4 Gy x 12 fractions over 4 weeks, without hyperthermia.

NCT06384053.schema_source: Open-access Trials protocol (PMC12723921); both radiotherapy schedules are stated in the abstract and full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SAFESTEREO is a multicenter randomized phase II trial comparing single- or three-fraction stereotactic radiosurgery with five-fraction treatment for brain metastases. The primary endpoint is local failure or radionecrosis at 2 years.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: One or more brain metastases from a solid tumor, age 18 or older, and Karnofsky performance status at least 70. Exclusions include small-cell lung cancer, germinoma, lymphoma, leptomeningeal disease, MRI contraindication, prior brain-metastasis surgery, and in-field reirradiation.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized between a standard short course and a five-fraction course.

arms.label: SRS
arms.text: 15-24 Gy in 1 or 3 fractions.

arms.label: Fractionated SRS
arms.text: 35 Gy in 5 fractions.

NCT05346367.schema_source: Open-access BMC Cancer paper (PMC10039548); eligibility and both dose schedules are from the methods.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SCIENCE (SCCH-TS2201) is a multicenter randomized phase III trial of three neoadjuvant strategies for locally advanced thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Planned enrolment is 420. Surgery is 6 to 8 weeks after neoadjuvant therapy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Allocation is 1:1:1. Chemotherapy in every arm is albumin-bound paclitaxel plus carboplatin on day 1 for two 3-week cycles. Sintilimab, when used, is given on day 1. Postoperative therapy is chosen by the investigator.

arms.label: Group A
arms.text: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus sintilimab, without radiotherapy.

arms.label: Group B
arms.text: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy plus sintilimab. Radiotherapy is IMRT, 41.4 Gy in 23 fractions, 5 days per week.

arms.label: Group C
arms.text: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy alone, with the same chemotherapy and the same 41.4 Gy in 23 fractions.

NCT05244798.schema_source: Open-access BMJ Open protocol (PMC12142158); the three regimens and 41.4 Gy schedule are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SCOPES-II is an international randomized phase II trial of two preoperative radiotherapy schedules for intermediate- or high-grade soft-tissue sarcoma of the head and neck, trunk, chest wall, or limbs. Planned enrolment is 150 adults.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Surgery is planned about 6 to 8 weeks after radiotherapy in both arms. The primary endpoint is wound complications within 120 days after surgery.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Preoperative radiotherapy, 14 fractions of 3 Gy.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Preoperative radiotherapy, 5 fractions of 6 Gy.

NCT07071727.schema_source: Open-access BMJ Open protocol (PMC13629992); both preoperative schedules are stated in the abstract.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized phase II trial of third-line therapy for microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer with liver metastases. Age 18-75. Allocation is 3:3:2. Primary endpoint is progression-free survival.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Liver radiotherapy, when assigned, is SBRT for oligometastases at 40-50 Gy in 5 fractions, 60-70 Gy in 10 fractions, or 65 Gy in 13 fractions. For multiple liver lesions, selected lesions receive that SBRT and the remaining liver lesions receive low-dose radiotherapy of 1-10 Gy total at 0.5-2.0 Gy per fraction.

arms.label: Intervention
arms.text: Sintilimab plus fruquintinib plus liver-directed radiotherapy.

arms.label: Control
arms.text: Sintilimab plus fruquintinib, without radiotherapy.

arms.label: Fruquintinib alone
arms.text: Fruquintinib monotherapy.

NCT06356584.schema_source: Open-access Frontiers in Immunology protocol (PMC13201437); the 3:3:2 arms and liver dose menus are from the abstract.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter randomized phase II trial for pathologically confirmed soft-tissue sarcoma at least 5 cm, ages 18-70. Planned enrolment is 106. Primary endpoint is objective response.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Allocation is 1:1.

arms.label: Conventional radiotherapy
arms.text: Uniform 3.0 Gy per fraction for 15-20 fractions.

arms.label: Spatially fractionated radiotherapy
arms.text: The conventional course plus high-dose spot irradiation of 8-15 Gy per fraction for 3-4 fractions.

NCT06980259.schema_source: Open-access Precision Radiation Oncology protocol (PMC13097558) registered to this NCT; both dose policies are in the abstract.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Protocol for bone metastases with soft-tissue formation, registered to this NCT. Patients are assigned to a conventional course or a core-boost course. Primary endpoint is objective response.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: The published methods describe assignment to two radiotherapy groups and state the doses. They do not describe stratification.

arms.label: Control
arms.text: Conventional radiotherapy, 30 Gy in 10 fractions.

arms.label: SFRT or SCART
arms.text: A single 8-12 Gy core dose using spatially fractionated radiotherapy or stereotactic core ablative radiotherapy, followed by 25-40 Gy in 5 fractions to the whole bone metastasis.

NCT06987370.schema_source: Open-access protocol (PMC12750312); the two dose schedules are taken from the abstract, which says patients are assigned to these groups.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SinocaRT is a multicenter randomized phase II trial after multi-block endoscopic endonasal surgery for sinonasal carcinoma. Planned enrolment is 52. Radiotherapy starts 4 to 8 weeks after surgery and is delivered over 7 weeks.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified by radiotherapy modality, photons versus protons.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Allocation is 1:1. High-risk volume is 60-66 Gy in 30-33 fractions for R0 or R1 margins, and 70 Gy in 35 fractions only for residual macroscopic tumor. Low-risk volume is 54.45 Gy at 1.65 Gy per fraction.

arms.label: Dose painting
arms.text: Dose painting by contours using histosurgical mapping of margin risk.

arms.label: Standard IMRT or IMPT
arms.text: Standard target delineation and optimization.

NCT05943119.schema_source: Open-access BMJ Open protocol (PMC13504533); randomization, stratification, and prescribed doses are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SMILE is an international phase III non-inferiority trial of two SBRT schedules for non-spine bone metastases. Planned enrolment is 162. Pain response is assessed at 3 months.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized to a 3-fraction or 5-fraction SBRT course.

arms.label: 3 fractions
arms.text: 9 Gy per fraction for 3 fractions.

arms.label: 5 fractions
arms.text: 7 Gy per fraction for 5 fractions.

NCT05406063.schema_source: Open-access Trials protocol (PMC11562624); both fraction doses are stated in the abstract.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SPARE is a single-arm phase II trial of stereotactic body proton therapy for primary renal cell carcinoma. Nineteen patients are followed for 2 years.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Biopsy-confirmed primary RCC when biopsy is feasible, medically inoperable or technically high risk for surgery or ablation, or declining those procedures, and no metastatic disease.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: There is no randomization.

arms.label: Proton SBRT
arms.text: Proton stereotactic body radiotherapy, 40-42 Gy in 3-5 fractions, planned on a four-dimensional CT.

NCT06376669.schema_source: Open-access BMC Cancer protocol (PMC12211292); the proton dose is stated in the methods.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized phase II trial of carbon-ion radiotherapy with or without a simultaneous integrated boost for localized prostate cancer. Planned enrolment is 140. Primary endpoint is grade 2 or higher acute toxicity.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Allocation is 1:1. In both arms, 95% of the prescription covers 100% of the CTV.

arms.label: Arm A carbon ions
arms.text: CTV 65.6 GyE in 16 fractions of 4.1 GyE over 4 weeks.

arms.label: Arm B carbon-ion boost
arms.text: The same CTV dose, 65.6 GyE in 16 fractions, with a simultaneous CTV boost of 72 GyE in 16 fractions of 4.5 GyE.

NCT05010343.schema_source: Open-access Trials protocol (PMC9644615); both carbon-ion prescriptions are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SPINAL is a multicenter randomized phase III non-inferiority trial of palliative spinal radiotherapy volume. The question is pain relief at day 30. Eligible adults have a painful spinal metastasis from C2 through S2.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Allocation is 1:1. Both arms use the same dose, chosen by the investigator: 8 Gy in 1 fraction or 20 Gy in 5 fractions, with static IMRT, VMAT, or helical tomotherapy.

arms.label: Standard volume
arms.text: The painful vertebral level, including the whole vertebra and any contiguous epidural disease, plus one vertebra above and one below.

arms.label: Reduced volume
arms.text: The same involved vertebra or vertebrae only, without the adjacent vertebral levels.

NCT06884332.schema_source: Open-access BMC Cancer protocol (PMC13245005); dose choices and the two CTV definitions are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SPORTSMEN is a three-arm randomized phase II trial of radiotherapy for symptomatic spine metastases. The primary endpoint is pain freedom at 3 months on the Brief Pain Inventory. About 240 patients are planned.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Three regimens are compared. The statistical methods state equal probability among the three arms. An earlier design paragraph states 2:1 between the combined SBRT arms and conventional radiotherapy.

arms.label: Two-fraction SBRT
arms.text: 24 Gy in 2 fractions.

arms.label: Single-fraction SBRT
arms.text: 19 Gy in 1 fraction.

arms.label: Conventional radiotherapy
arms.text: 8 Gy in 1 fraction.

schema.note: The published protocol contains both allocation statements.

NCT05617716.schema_source: Open-access Reports of Practical Oncology and Radiotherapy protocol (PMC10547410); the three doses are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SIMPLIFY-SABR-COMET is a phase III 1:1 non-inferiority trial of single-fraction versus multi-fraction SABR for 1-5 oligometastases or oligoprogressive lesions. Planned enrolment is 598. A second 1:1 randomization at BC Cancer sites compares quality-of-life questionnaires alone with symptom-guided clinician intervention.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: The fractionation randomization is stratified by systemic therapy within the prior 2 weeks, one versus multiple SABR sites, and abdominal SABR yes versus no. The questionnaire randomization is stratified by sex.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Bracketed doses are protocol alternate options. Brain dose is institutional in both arms.

arms.label: Multi-fraction SABR
arms.text: Lung away from mediastinum or plexus: 48 Gy in 4 (alternate 54 Gy in 3). Lung within 2 cm: 60 Gy in 8 (alternate 50 Gy in 5). Non-spine bone: 35 Gy in 5. Liver: 54 Gy in 3 (alternate 50 Gy in 5). Spine: 24 Gy in 2 (alternate 35 Gy in 5). Adrenal, node, or soft tissue: 40 Gy in 5 (alternate 35 Gy in 5).

arms.label: Single-fraction SABR
arms.text: Peripheral lung 30 Gy (alternate 34 Gy). Lung within 2 cm of mediastinum or plexus: 20 Gy. Liver 30 Gy (alternate 34 Gy). Bone, spine, adrenal, node, or soft tissue: 20 Gy.

NCT05784428.schema_source: Open-access BMC Cancer protocol (PMC10838428); fractionation tables and stratification are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: STEREO-HBM is a multicenter two-step non-randomized phase II trial for brain metastases with recent hemorrhage. At least one of up to 3 brain metastases must be hemorrhagic. A postoperative bed may also be treated.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Small-cell lung cancer, germ-cell tumors, lymphoma, melanoma, leukemia, and myeloma are excluded.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: There is no randomization.

arms.label: Fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy
arms.text: Each target receives 30 Gy in 3 fractions of 10 Gy, every other day, preferably within 1 week and no longer than 7-10 days.

NCT03696680.schema_source: Open-access BMC Cancer protocol (PMC7036220); the 30 Gy in 3 fractions regimen is from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: STEREOPAC is a multicenter randomized phase II trial for borderline-resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Planned enrolment is 256. Everyone starts with 4 cycles of mFOLFIRINOX or 6 doses of gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization, limited to patients without progression and with manageable tolerance, is minimized by center and CA 19-9.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: After restaging, non-progressive patients are randomized. Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel may replace mFOLFIRINOX for intolerance. Isotoxic SBRT is 5 daily fractions, escalated until an organ constraint is reached, with maximum dose to 0.5 cc below 55 Gy.

arms.label: Arm A chemotherapy
arms.text: Four further mFOLFIRINOX cycles, or 6 further gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel doses, then surgery.

arms.label: Arm B chemotherapy plus SBRT
arms.text: Two mFOLFIRINOX cycles or 3 gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel doses, then isotoxic high-dose SBRT (35 to 55 Gy in 5 fractions), then two further mFOLFIRINOX cycles or 3 gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel doses, then surgery.

NCT05083247.schema_source: Open-access BMC Cancer protocol (PMC10512504); the sequence, SBRT dose range, and stratification are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: STEREOSARC is a multicenter randomized phase II trial of multisite SBRT with or without atezolizumab for oligorecurrent soft-tissue sarcoma. Planned enrolment is 103. Maximum cumulative tumor diameter is 6 cm.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Allocation is 2:1, experimental to control. SBRT uses 3 fractions in favorable cases and 5 fractions when organs are close. The protocol does not state the gray per fraction. SBRT and atezolizumab start the same day, with SBRT first.

arms.label: SBRT plus atezolizumab
arms.text: SBRT plus atezolizumab 1200 mg every 3 weeks for six cycles.

arms.label: SBRT alone
arms.text: SBRT without atezolizumab.

NCT03548428.schema_source: Open-access BMJ Open protocol (PMC7513631); the 2:1 design, atezolizumab schedule, and fraction counts are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized phase III comparison of preoperative versus postoperative single-fraction stereotactic radiosurgery for a resectable brain metastasis, with radiosurgery also planned for all lesions requiring treatment when there are fewer than 10 metastases. About 116 evaluable patients are required.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Age 18 or older, solid-tumor brain metastasis with a surgical indication for one lesion, and ECOG 0-2.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Age under 60 versus 60 or older; 1 versus 2-4 versus 5-10 brain metastases; resection under 3.0 cm versus larger than 3.0 cm but under 5.0 cm; lung versus radioresistant histology (melanoma, renal cell carcinoma, sarcoma) versus other; dural contact yes versus no; linac versus Gamma Knife.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Dynamic 1:1 allocation. Dose is a single fraction by lesion volume: under 4.2 cc, 20 Gy (22 Gy allowed for subcentimeter lesions); 4.2 to under 8.0 cc, 18 Gy; 8.0 to under 14.4 cc, 17 Gy; 14.4 to under 20 cc, 15 Gy; 20 to under 30 cc, 14 Gy; 30 cc or larger, maximum 12 Gy.

arms.label: Preoperative SRS
arms.text: SRS to the contrast-enhancing metastasis, then surgery within 2 weeks. GTV equals CTV, with an optional 1 mm expansion for dural contact.

arms.label: Postoperative SRS
arms.text: Surgery first, then SRS to the surgical bed plus 1 mm within 4 weeks.

NCT05545007.schema_source: Open-access BMC Cancer protocol (PMC10929171), which cites this NCT; sequence, stratification, and volume-based doses are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: INVERT is a phase II randomized trial of involved-nodal versus elective-neck radiotherapy for oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx squamous cell carcinoma, AJCC stage I-IVB, ECOG 0-2. Planned enrolment is 80.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Allocation is 1:1. Every patient receives 70 Gy in 35 fractions to gross disease and 63 Gy in 35 fractions to suspicious nodes.

arms.label: Elective neck irradiation
arms.text: Elective neck 56 Gy, plus the common gross-disease and suspicious-node doses.

arms.label: Involved nodal radiotherapy
arms.text: Elective neck irradiation is omitted. Additional nodes flagged by the trial radiomics model receive 56 Gy to the node only.

NCT06477692.schema_source: Open-access BMC Cancer protocol (PMC13335197); the 70, 63, and 56 Gy volumes are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SUCLANODE is a multicenter randomized phase III trial of medial versus entire supraclavicular irradiation after breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy. Target enrolment is 1650.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: High risk means pathologic N2-3b after surgery first, or clinical stage III or pathologic N1-3b after neoadjuvant systemic therapy.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Neoadjuvant versus adjuvant systemic therapy, T3-4 versus T1-2, N3 versus not N3, and estrogen-receptor positive versus negative.

schema.label: Randomize

arms.label: Medial supraclavicular irradiation

arms.label: Regional radiotherapy

schema.label: Entry

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized to one versus five fractions.

arms.label: Single fraction

NCT06885671.schema_source: Open-access Clinical and Translational Radiation Oncology paper (PMC12333179); both partial-breast doses are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SIOP Ependymoma II enrols patients younger than 22 years with centrally confirmed ependymoma after biopsy or resection. Three randomized strata depend on age, residual disease, and suitability for radiotherapy. Patients outside those strata are observed.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Program entry is stratified by age, tumor location, and the result of the initial surgery.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Stratum I is age at least 12 months with no measurable residual disease. Stratum II is older than 1 year with measurable inoperable residual WHO grade II-III ependymoma and no metastasis. Stratum III is younger than 12 months, or younger than 18 months in the UK, or otherwise not eligible for radiotherapy.

arms.label: Stratum I observation
arms.text: Complete resection and conformal radiotherapy without maintenance chemotherapy.

arms.label: Stratum I chemotherapy
arms.text: The same resection and conformal radiotherapy, followed by 16 weeks of VEC (vincristine, etoposide, cyclophosphamide) plus cisplatin.

arms.label: Stratum II VEC
arms.text: Postoperative VEC, with second-look surgery considered. An 8 Gy boost after conformal radiotherapy is studied if residual disease remains. The conformal dose is not stated in the sections read.

arms.label: Stratum II VEC plus methotrexate
arms.text: Postoperative VEC plus high-dose methotrexate, with the same second-look and 8 Gy boost policy.

arms.label: Stratum III chemotherapy
arms.text: Alternating myelosuppressive and non-myelosuppressive chemotherapy without valproate.

arms.label: Stratum III chemotherapy plus valproate
arms.text: The same chemotherapy plus valproate.

NCT02265770.schema_source: Open-access Frontiers in Oncology protocol (PMC9201444); the three randomized comparisons and the 8 Gy boost are from the full text.

arms.label: Neoadjuvant protons

schema.text: RENALUT is a multicenter single-arm phase II trial of PSMA radioligand therapy for metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma after tyrosine-kinase inhibitor and immune-checkpoint inhibitor failure. About 56 patients are screened to enrol 48.

schema.label: Entry

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: There is no randomization. The abstract does not state the activity in GBq.

arms.label: Lu-177 PSMA-617

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SCR-ESCC-01 is a randomized phase II trial of first-line immunochemotherapy with or without radiotherapy for metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both arms use a PD-1 inhibitor with paclitaxel and platinum every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, then immunotherapy maintenance for up to 24 months.

arms.text: Before each of the 4 immunochemotherapy cycles, low-dose radiotherapy of 2 Gy x 2 fractions to the primary tumor and all metastases, then conventional radiotherapy of 40-50 Gy in 20-25 fractions to the primary tumor starting at the fifth immunotherapy cycle.

arms.label: Arm B systemic therapy

NCT05978193.schema_source: Schema taken from the Future Oncology abstract (PMID 37937444), which states both arms; the full text was not open access.

schema.text: RO-PIP is a multicenter randomized feasibility trial of reirradiation for prostate cancer that recurred inside the prostate after prior radiotherapy. The target was 60 participants at three centers over 24 months.

schema.label: Randomize

arms.label: HDR brachytherapy
arms.text: High-dose-rate brachytherapy.

arms.label: SBRT
arms.text: Stereotactic body radiotherapy.

NCT05614700.schema_source: Schema taken from the abstract of the feasibility report (PMID 41812301), which names the randomized modalities; doses were not in the abstract and the full text was not open.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: STRONG II is a single-arm multicenter phase II trial adding SBRT after chemotherapy for non-metastatic unresectable perihilar cholangiocarcinoma, T1-4 and N0-2. Planned enrolment is 30.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: There is no randomization.

arms.label: Chemotherapy then SBRT
arms.text: SBRT in 15 fractions of 4.0-4.5 Gy, added to chemotherapy.

NCT06493734.schema_source: Open-access BMJ Open protocol (PMC12273127); the SBRT schedule is stated in the abstract.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: TORPEDO is a multicenter randomized phase II trial for inoperable non-metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, including borderline-resectable disease that is medically inoperable or when surgery is declined.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified by chemotherapy regimen, modified FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, and by locally advanced versus borderline-resectable disease.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: After 12 weeks of induction chemotherapy, patients without distant progression are randomized 1:1.

arms.label: Arm A chemotherapy
arms.text: Continued modified FOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel.

arms.label: Arm B chemotherapy plus SBRT
arms.text: One further month of the same chemotherapy, then SBRT 8 Gy x 5 fractions. Chemotherapy may continue after SBRT.

NCT06691425.schema_source: Open-access BMC Cancer protocol (PMC12574135); induction, stratification, and the 5 x 8 Gy SBRT arm are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: VoiceS is a multicenter randomized phase III superiority trial for untreated unilateral stage 0 or I glottic cancer (cTis or cT1a). Planned enrolment is 34. The primary endpoint is voice handicap index from 6 to 24 months.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized to single-vocal-cord irradiation or laser cordectomy.

arms.label: Single vocal cord irradiation
arms.text: 16 fractions of 3.63 Gy (58.08 Gy) to the involved vocal cord, using IMRT or VMAT.

arms.label: Laser cordectomy
arms.text: Transoral CO2-laser cordectomy, European Laryngological Society type I-IV, within 3 weeks after randomization.

NCT04057209.schema_source: Open-access BMC Cancer protocol (PMC9615245); the 16 x 3.63 Gy schedule and cordectomy arm are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: TURBO is a single-center randomized phase II non-inferiority trial of two-fraction versus five-fraction MR-linac radiotherapy for intermediate-risk localized prostate cancer. Planned enrolment is 160, randomized 1:1. Data are collected in MOMENTUM.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: The primary endpoint is grade 2 or higher acute genitourinary toxicity through 90 days.

arms.label: Five fractions
arms.text: 36.25 Gy in 5 fractions over 16-18 days.

arms.label: Two fractions with boost
arms.text: 12 Gy x 2 to the prostate over 8 days, with a simultaneous boost up to 13.5 Gy per fraction to the gross tumor (24 Gy to the prostate and up to 27 Gy to the tumor).

NCT06518226.schema_source: Open-access Trials protocol (PMC12751598); both prostate schedules are stated in the abstract and full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: ULTRAS is a multicenter phase III randomized trial of two single-fraction MR-guided SBRT doses for liver oligometastases or oligoprogression. Planned enrolment is 114, with 2 years of follow-up.

schema.label: Stratify

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Allocation is 1:1. The primary endpoint is local control of the treated intrahepatic lesion.

arms.label: High-dose single fraction
arms.text: 27 Gy in 1 fraction.

arms.label: Ultra-high-dose single fraction

NCT06362395.schema_source: Schema taken from the Contemporary Clinical Trials abstract (PMID 42309387); the full text was not open access.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: TORCH-E is a multicenter single-arm phase II trial of total neoadjuvant therapy for cT1-3bN0M0 low rectal cancer, followed by surgery or watch-and-wait. Planned enrolment is 34.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: There is no randomization.

arms.label: Short-course RT then chemo-immunotherapy
arms.text: 25 Gy in 5 fractions, then four cycles of capecitabine, oxaliplatin, and toripalimab, then surgery or watch-and-wait.

NCT05555888.schema_source: Open-access BMJ Open protocol (PMC10565143); the 25 Gy schedule and drug sequence are from the abstract.

schema.text: TORCH-LE is a multicenter single-arm phase II trial for microsatellite-stable early rectal cancer with high-risk features after local excision, when completion total mesorectal excision is refused or not feasible. Planned enrolment is 60.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: There is no randomization.

arms.label: Short-course RT then CapeOx and toripalimab
arms.text: 25 Gy in 5 fractions, then four cycles of capecitabine plus oxaliplatin and toripalimab.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: TAUTEM-T1 is a multicenter randomized phase III superiority trial of preoperative chemoradiotherapy plus transanal endoscopic microsurgery versus local excision alone for cT1N0M0 rectal adenocarcinoma. Allocation is 1:1. Primary endpoint is rectal preservation at 3 years.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Adults with biopsy-proven low- or moderate-grade adenocarcinoma 4 cm or smaller, less than 10 cm from the anal verge, staged cT1N0M0.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Local excision is at week 10 in the chemoradiotherapy arm. Watch-and-wait is not allowed. Capecitabine is 825 mg/m2 every 12 hours on radiotherapy days. VMAT is preferred.

arms.label: Chemoradiotherapy then local excision
arms.text: VMAT: 45 Gy in 25 fractions to tumor, mesorectum, and regional nodes, with an integrated boost of 50 Gy in 25 fractions to the tumor and any pathologic adjacent nodes. If 3D conformal radiotherapy is used: 45 Gy in 25 fractions then a sequential 5.4 Gy in 3 fractions. Concurrent capecitabine, then transanal endoscopic microsurgery.

arms.label: Local excision alone
arms.text: Transanal endoscopic microsurgery without preoperative chemoradiotherapy.

NCT06450574.schema_source: Open-access International Journal of Colorectal Disease protocol (PMC13236827); randomization and both radiotherapy schedules are from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: TARGET phase II randomized trial of tyrosine-kinase inhibitor alone versus the same inhibitor plus local consolidative radiotherapy for EGFR- or ALK-mutated oligometastatic non-small-cell lung cancer. Patients start a TKI, and those without progression after 2-4 months are randomized. Planned enrolment is 106.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Up to 5 oligometastatic sites at presentation, ECOG 0-2.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Number of oligometastatic sites, 1-3 versus 4-5; performance status 0-1 versus 2; and brain metastases.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Allocation is 1:1. Radiotherapy starts within 4 weeks. A lesion in complete response, or too small to plan, is observed rather than irradiated. The protocol refers dose menus to a table that was not transcribed here.

arms.label: TKI alone
arms.text: Continue the EGFR or ALK tyrosine-kinase inhibitor.

arms.label: TKI plus local radiotherapy
arms.text: Continue the TKI and add local consolidative radiotherapy to the primary, involved regional nodes, and oligometastases.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Phase III randomized trial of maintenance therapy with or without local consolidative radiotherapy after at least 4-6 cycles of systemic therapy without progression, for non-small-cell lung cancer with 1-5 metastatic sites. Planned enrolment is 190.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Pathologic NSCLC, ECOG 0-2, metastases suitable for SBRT, and the primary suitable for definitive radiotherapy. Up to 3 lesions in one organ are allowed. The primary tumor and regional nodes are not counted in the 1-5.

schema.text: The randomization section stratifies by 1-2 versus 3-5 metastatic sites, nodal status N0-N1 versus N2, and brain metastases present versus absent.

arms.label: Maintenance alone
arms.text: Chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or observation, started 4-8 weeks after randomization.

arms.label: Radiotherapy plus maintenance
arms.text: SBRT to every oligometastasis plus definitive radiotherapy to the primary and involved nodes, 45-55 Gy in 15-22 fractions as normal tissue allows, started within 4 weeks. Maintenance may be concurrent or within 4 weeks after radiotherapy.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: TROG 21.07 SOCRATES-HCC is a phase II open-label randomized trial for newly diagnosed solitary hepatocellular carcinoma up to 8 cm, BCLC 0 or A, Child-Pugh A or B7, and not suitable for resection or transplantation. Two cohorts are randomized separately.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Solitary nodule, no plan for transplant, and clinically compensated cirrhosis. All primary therapy starts within 28 days of randomization and finishes within 42 days.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Within each cohort, randomization is stratified by Child-Pugh A versus B7 and by BCLC stage 0 versus A.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Cohort 1 (target 118) is tumors 3 cm or smaller that are eligible for percutaneous thermal ablation. Cohort 2 (target 100) is tumors 3 cm or smaller that are ineligible for ablation, or tumors larger than 3 cm up to 8 cm.

arms.label: Cohort 1 ablation
arms.text: Microwave or radiofrequency ablation, aiming for a margin greater than 5 mm, with completion confirmed on contrast CT.

arms.label: Cohort 1 SABR
arms.text: SABR. For Child-Pugh A without a dose-limiting organ, 50 Gy in 5 fractions or 42-45 Gy in 3 fractions is recommended. Child-Pugh B7 without a dose-limiting organ: 40-50 Gy in 5 fractions preferred, or 36 Gy in 3. If an organ limits dose: 35-40 Gy in 5 fractions.

arms.label: Cohort 2 SABR
arms.text: Same SABR dose policy as cohort 1.

arms.label: Cohort 2 other standard care
arms.text: Transarterial chemoembolization or radioembolization. Thermal ablation, including combined procedures, is allowed for tumors larger than 3 cm when that is institutional standard care.

schema.text: Cohort 1 (target 118) is tumors 3 cm or smaller that are eligible for percutaneous thermal ablation. Cohort 2 (target 100) is tumors 3 cm or smaller that are ineligible for ablation, or tumors larger than 3 cm up to 8 cm.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Open-label single-arm phase II study of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT-guided maximal cytoreduction plus apalutamide and androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for newly diagnosed oligometastatic metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Men 18 years or older with histologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma, newly diagnosed disease, at most 10 distant metastases on conventional imaging, ECOG 0-1, and a PSMA PET/CT within 6 weeks before apalutamide plus ADT. schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: There is no randomization. Every patient receives apalutamide 240 mg orally once daily, with dose adjustment for intolerance, plus ADT for 6 cycles.

arms.label: Apalutamide plus ADT, then response-adapted local therapy
arms.text: After 3 cycles, patients who still have oligometastatic disease on PSMA PET/CT undergo cytoreductive radical prostatectomy. PSMA PET/CT-guided metastasis-directed external-beam radiotherapy is given at investigator discretion. Apalutamide plus ADT continues for 2 weeks after surgery.
