schema.label: Design
schema.text: Open-label multicenter phase III trial comparing fractionated proton therapy with fractionated photon radiotherapy for cavernous sinus benign meningioma. The primary endpoint is cognitive or functional deterioration at 5 years. Planned enrollment is 160 patients, 80 per arm.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Adults older than 18 and younger than 60 years with a grade 1 cavernous sinus meningioma, or an anterior skull-base meningioma invading the cavernous sinus, whose clinical target volume is larger than 3 cm. Adjuvant or exclusive irradiation is allowed. Radiosurgery and hypofractionated regimens are excluded. WHO performance status 0-1.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified by age, sex, and Montreal Cognitive Assessment score.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Eligible patients are randomized 1:1. Both arms use conventional fractionation of 1.8 Gy (RBE) per fraction. The protocol does not assign a different total dose by arm.

arms.label: Proton therapy
arms.text: Fractionated proton therapy at 1.8 Gy (RBE) per fraction.

arms.label: Photon radiotherapy
arms.text: Fractionated photon radiotherapy at 1.8 Gy (RBE) per fraction.

NCT05895344.schema_source: Open-access COG-PROTON-01 protocol (BMC Cancer, 2024) states the 1:1 proton versus photon randomization, stratification, and 1.8 Gy per fraction requirement.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized open-label phase Ib multi-arm platform trial of DNA-damage-response inhibitors with fixed-dose radical radiotherapy for locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer unsuitable for concurrent chemoradiotherapy. Separate time-to-event continual reassessment models escalate each inhibitor.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: The platform tests inhibitors directed at PARP, ATR, Wee1, ATM, and DNA-PK. Radiotherapy starts 7 days after the first inhibitor dose and is intensity-modulated or volumetric modulated arc therapy with daily cone-beam CT. A 5 mm internal-target margin and a further 5 mm planning-target margin are used.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized between the open experimental arm and a radiotherapy-alone calibration cohort. Radiotherapy-alone patients are pooled as contemporary controls and are not the primary comparison. As of the 2022 design report, two arms were open.

arms.label: Radiotherapy alone
arms.text: Radical thoracic radiotherapy, 60 Gy in 30 daily 2 Gy fractions over about 40 days.

arms.label: CONCORDE-A, olaparib
arms.text: Olaparib, a PARP inhibitor, given with the same 60 Gy in 30 fractions. Six dose levels are incorporated, limited by available tablet strengths.

arms.label: CONCORDE-B, AZD1390
arms.text: AZD1390, an ATM inhibitor, given with the same 60 Gy in 30 fractions. Daily and intermittent dose levels are included because it is a more potent radiosensitizer than olaparib.

schema.note: The 2022 report plans about 150 patients on inhibitor plus radiotherapy and up to 60 on radiotherapy alone if five experimental arms accrue.

NCT04550104.schema_source: Open-access CONCORDE protocol (Clinical and Translational Radiation Oncology, 2020) and the 2022 TiTE-CRM implementation paper name the 60 Gy radiotherapy backbone, the calibration arm, olaparib, and AZD1390.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Swedish multicenter randomized phase II trial with a patient-preference design. It compares contact X-ray brachytherapy plus chemoradiotherapy with contact X-ray brachytherapy plus short-course radiotherapy for organ preservation in early-to-intermediate rectal cancer. Target enrollment is 110 patients, 55 per arm.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Operable patients 18 years or older with cT1 to cT3ab tumors smaller than 5 cm, involving less than half the rectal circumference, N0 to N1 with at most 3 nodes smaller than 8 mm, within 10 cm of the anal verge, and M0 or MX.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Stratification factors are treatment center, cT1-T2 versus cT3a-b, tumor diameter less than 3 cm versus 3 cm or larger, and distance from the anal verge less than 6 cm versus 6 to 10 cm.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Participants are randomized 1:1. Investigators are not blinded. If the tumor is smaller than 3 cm, contact X-ray brachytherapy is given first. If it is 3 cm or larger, external radiotherapy is given first and contact therapy follows after a rest.

arms.label: Arm A, contact therapy plus chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: Contact X-ray brachytherapy 90 Gy in three fractions of 30 Gy, 2 weeks apart, plus chemoradiotherapy 45 to 50 Gy in 1.8 to 2 Gy fractions over 5 weeks with capecitabine 900 mg/m2 twice daily.

arms.label: Arm B, contact therapy plus short-course radiotherapy
arms.text: The same contact X-ray brachytherapy, 90 Gy in three fractions of 30 Gy, plus short-course radiotherapy 25 Gy in five daily fractions.

NCT06501053.schema_source: Open-access CORRECT protocol (BMJ Open, 2025) states the preference design, stratification, and both contact-radiotherapy arms.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter randomized open-label phase III trial for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma with oligoprogression during first-line systemic therapy. Planned enrollment is 132 patients, 66 per arm. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified by oligoprogression subtype: repeat oligoprogression versus induced oligoprogression.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1. Radiotherapy, when used, should reach a biologically effective dose of at least 60 Gy (alpha/beta 10) when feasible, and all eligible oligoprogressive lesions should be treated within 3 months.

arms.label: Continue first-line therapy plus radiotherapy
arms.text: Continue the same first-line systemic regimen and add radiotherapy to all oligoprogressive lesions. For stereotactic body radiotherapy, 7 to 10 Gy per fraction for five fractions is recommended. Non-stereotactic plans should still reach a biologically effective dose of at least 60 Gy.

arms.label: Early switch to second-line therapy
arms.text: Stop first-line systemic therapy and start second-line systemic therapy without protocol radiotherapy.

NCT06841172.schema_source: Open-access CROSS protocol (BMJ Open, 2026) states the 1:1 randomization, the oligoprogression stratification, and both systemic-therapy strategies.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Investigator-initiated prospective single-arm phase II trial at Princess Margaret Cancer Centre testing whether stereotactic or hypofractionated radiotherapy to oligoprogressive sites can prolong progression-free survival while first-line systemic therapy continues.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Metastatic melanoma with at most 10 extracranial oligoprogressive lesions during first-line systemic therapy, including anti-PD-1 monotherapy or combination therapy. Brain-only progression, untreated or symptomatic central nervous system disease, and leptomeningeal disease are excluded. Previously irradiated lesions may be retreated if safe.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: There is no randomization. Systemic therapy continues and every oligoprogressive lesion is irradiated.

arms.label: Continue systemic therapy plus ablative radiotherapy
arms.text: Stereotactic body radiotherapy or single-fraction hypofractionated radiotherapy to all oligoprogressive lesions. The default dose is 8 to 10 Gy for 3 fractions, or 8 to 10 Gy in 1 fraction. Other schedules are allowed when safer for the lesion.

NCT07112170.schema_source: Open-access CURB-Melanoma protocol (Frontiers in Oncology, 2026) states the single-arm design and the default oligoprogression radiotherapy doses.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized phase III Danish Breast Cancer Group Proton Trial. Patients whose photon plan would give a high heart or lung dose in order to cover locoregional targets, including internal mammary nodes, are randomized between photon radiotherapy and proton therapy. No proton-versus-photon plan comparison is required before randomization.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: The radiotherapy committee set the selection thresholds at mean heart dose of at least 4 Gy and/or ipsilateral lung V17Gy (hypofractionated plans) or V20Gy (normofractionated plans) of at least 37%. Target coverage may be compromised only after randomization in the photon plan, reflecting usual practice.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Selected patients are randomized between the two modalities. The prescribed dose in the reported treated cohort was either 50 Gy in 25 fractions or 40 Gy in 15 fractions. Five of the first 43 proton-treated patients also received a simultaneous integrated tumor-bed boost.

arms.label: Photon radiotherapy
arms.text: Photon locoregional radiotherapy at the prescribed 50 Gy in 25 fractions or 40 Gy in 15 fractions.

arms.label: Proton therapy
arms.text: Proton locoregional radiotherapy at the same prescribed dose, delivered with 2 to 3 en face fields, single-field optimization, and robust optimization.

NCT04291378.schema_source: The open-access selection-criteria paper states photon versus proton randomization and the heart and lung thresholds, and the 2022 planning abstract states the 50 Gy and 40 Gy prescriptions.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Danish Breast Cancer Group RT Natural trial of partial breast irradiation versus no radiotherapy after breast-conserving surgery for selected low-risk breast cancer in older women.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Women 60 years or older with a unilateral, unifocal, non-lobular invasive carcinoma no larger than 20 mm, pathologically node negative, hormone-receptor positive, and HER2 normal. Isolated tumor cells are allowed. Micrometastases, prior breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ, known hereditary breast cancer, and prior breast or chest-wall radiotherapy exclude patients.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Eligible patients are randomized 1:1. Patients who decline randomization because they prefer no radiotherapy may enroll in a separate self-selected no-radiotherapy cohort.

arms.label: Partial breast irradiation
arms.text: Partial breast irradiation, 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks, using the DBCG partial-breast volumes consistent with IMPORT LOW definitions.

arms.label: No radiotherapy
arms.text: No breast radiotherapy. All patients are offered annual screening mammography for 10 years.

NCT03646955.schema_source: Open-access radiotherapy quality-assurance report of the DBCG RT Natural trial (2026) states the 1:1 randomization and the 40 Gy partial-breast versus no-radiotherapy arms.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Open-label single-center phase II trial of hypoxia-directed dose escalation using fluoromisonidazole PET/CT in head and neck cancer planned for radical radiotherapy, with or without concurrent chemotherapy.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: A baseline fluoromisonidazole PET/CT classifies tumors by tumor-to-muscle ratio. Normoxic tumors (ratio below 1.4) are Arm 1, an external standard-care cohort, and are not part of the randomized comparison.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Hypoxic patients (ratio 1.4 or higher) are stratified by T stage, N stage, and tumor site.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Hypoxic patients are randomized 1:1 to Arm 2 or Arm 3. Both receive IMRT and concurrent cisplatin 40 mg/m2.

arms.label: Arm 1, normoxic external cohort
arms.text: Standard care, not included in the primary randomized comparison.

arms.label: Arm 2, standard chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: 70 Gy in 2 Gy fractions with concurrent cisplatin.

arms.label: Arm 3, hypoxic boost
arms.text: The Arm 2 regimen plus an additional 10 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction to the hypoxic subvolume plus a 5 mm isotropic margin, for a total of 80 Gy.

NCT06087614.schema_source: Open-access DEHyART protocol (ecancer, 2025) states the hypoxia threshold, stratification, cisplatin dose, and 70 Gy versus 80 Gy arms.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective multicenter open-label single-arm trial of personalized de-escalation of elective nodal volumes in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint is out-of-field nodal recurrence at 2 years. The target is 120 patients at six Swiss centers.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients receive definitive radiotherapy and, when indicated, standard-of-care chemotherapy. Prior head and neck surgery, chemotherapy, or radiotherapy is not allowed, except a single diagnostic lymph-node excision or treatment of Tis-T2 glottic cancer that did not treat the neck.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: There is no randomization. The study intervention is the elective clinical target volume. Primary-tumor dose follows standard care.

arms.label: Personalized elective nodal radiotherapy
arms.text: Simultaneous integrated boost in 30 to 35 fractions: CTV-1/PTV-1 65 to 70 Gy, optional CTV-2/PTV-2 60 to 66 Gy, and elective CTV-3/PTV-3 50 to 56 Gy. Elective levels are chosen from T stage, midline extension, and involved levels, including omission of the contralateral neck for fully lateralized tumors and sparing of levels I and V in many patients.

NCT06563362.schema_source: Open-access DeEscO protocol (Clinical and Translational Radiation Oncology, 2026) states the single-arm volume rules and the dose ranges.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter prospective phase II trial of FDG PET/CT staging to allocate, not randomize, treatment in muscle-invasive bladder cancer. All patients receive standard radical local therapy and neoadjuvant chemotherapy when eligible. Target enrollment is 156.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Histologically proven muscle-invasive bladder cancer, or at least T3 on conventional imaging, planned for radical treatment, with no extra-pelvic metastases on conventional thoracic and abdominopelvic imaging. A second PET/CT is used when neoadjuvant chemotherapy is given, and allocation uses the scan with the most distant metastases.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are not randomized. After a negative conventional metastatic workup, FDG PET/CT assigns the treatment intensification.

arms.label: Arm 1, PET M0
arms.text: Radical cystectomy with extended pelvic lymph-node dissection, or trimodality therapy with visibly complete resection plus 55 Gy in 20 fractions to the bladder and a radiosensitizer.

arms.label: Arm 2, one to three PET metastases
arms.text: The same radical local therapy plus metastasis-directed therapy. Both surgery and stereotactic body radiotherapy are allowed for the oligometastases.

arms.label: Arm 3, more than three PET metastases
arms.text: The same radical local therapy plus systemic immunotherapy. The immunotherapy regimen follows current guidelines and reimbursement and is not fixed in the protocol.

NCT04724928.schema_source: Open-access EFFORT-MIBC protocol (BMC Cancer, 2021) states the PET-based allocation and the local therapy, metastasis-directed therapy, and immunotherapy arms.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter open-label randomized phase III trial of total neoadjuvant therapy for locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma. The primary endpoint is organ-preservation-adapted disease-free survival.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Adults with ECOG 0-1 and rectal adenocarcinoma at most 12 cm from the anal verge, clinical stage II (cT3-4N0M0) or III (any T, N1-2, M0).

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Minimization uses institution, clinical T stage (cT1-3 versus cT4), clinical N status (negative versus positive), and distance from the anal verge (less than 5 cm versus 5 cm or more).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1. Both arms start with short-course radiotherapy, 25 Gy in 5 fractions. Chemotherapy starts 1 to 3 weeks later, up to 4 weeks allowed, for six cycles every 3 weeks.

arms.label: CAPOX
arms.text: Capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 orally twice daily on days 1 to 14 and oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1.

arms.label: CAPOXIRI
arms.text: Capecitabine 800 mg/m2 orally twice daily on days 1 to 14, oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1, and irinotecan 200 mg/m2 on day 1. From 26 August 2023 the irinotecan starting dose was 150 mg/m2, with an optional increase to 200 mg/m2 after course 2.

NCT05646511.schema_source: Open-access ENSEMBLE trial report (Japanese Journal of Clinical Oncology) states the minimization factors and the CAPOX versus CAPOXIRI regimens after short-course radiotherapy.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective single-center phase II study of focal salvage brachytherapy for prostate cancer recurring in part of the gland after prior radiotherapy. The primary endpoint is grade 3 or higher genitourinary or gastrointestinal toxicity.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: At least 24 months after radical radiotherapy, low toxicity from that treatment, and International Prostate Symptom Score below 20. The target is the biopsy-confirmed dominant lesion on MRI and/or PET, not the whole gland.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: There is no randomization. The isotope and dose rate are chosen from the prior radiotherapy so that salvage treatment does not repeat the same dose rate.

arms.label: HDR focal salvage
arms.text: After external-beam radiotherapy given at less than 3 Gy per fraction, iridium-192 high-dose-rate brachytherapy, 26 Gy in two fractions of 13 Gy, 3 to 14 days apart, to the clinical target volume.

arms.label: Ultra-low-dose-rate focal salvage
arms.text: After external-beam radiotherapy above 3 Gy per fraction, stereotactic body radiotherapy, or prior high-dose-rate brachytherapy, iodine-125 seeds deliver 145 Gy to the clinical target volume.

NCT05715502.schema_source: Open-access FocaSaBra trial-design paper (2026) states the prior-radiotherapy rule and the 26 Gy high-dose-rate and 145 Gy seed prescriptions.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective randomized open-label phase 2 umbrella trial of precision neoadjuvant therapy for early breast cancer. Patients are first divided by hormone-receptor and HER2 status. Within each subtype they are assigned to a precision regimen or an active comparator. The design paper specifies both 1:1 randomization and Bayesian adaptive randomization for drug assignment.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Women with unilateral primary invasive breast cancer who are candidates for neoadjuvant therapy. The published HR-positive/HER2-negative cohort required stage T2-4, N0-2, M0 and ECOG 0-1. HR-positive/HER2-negative tumors are subtyped by similarity-network fusion into SNF1 through SNF4.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: In the HR-positive/HER2-negative cohort, SNF1 is the endocrine-based group and SNF2-4 are the targeted-based group. Each group is randomized 1:1. PCb is nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 plus carboplatin AUC 1.5, each on days 1, 8, and 15 of a 28-day cycle, for six cycles.

arms.label: SNF1 endocrine precision
arms.text: Dalpiciclib 150 mg orally on days 1 to 21 plus letrozole 2.5 mg daily, with goserelin 3.6 mg intramuscularly every 4 weeks if premenopausal, for six 28-day cycles.

arms.label: SNF1 control
arms.text: PCb for six cycles.

arms.label: SNF2 precision
arms.text: SHR-1316 10 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 15 plus PCb for six cycles.

arms.label: SNF3 precision
arms.text: Fuzuloparib 50 mg orally twice daily plus PCb for six cycles.

arms.label: SNF4 precision
arms.text: Apatinib 250 mg orally daily plus PCb for six cycles.

arms.label: SNF2-4 control
arms.text: PCb for six cycles.

arms.label: HER2-positive precision
arms.text: SHR-A1811 4.8 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 every 3 weeks for eight cycles, with or without pyrotinib 240 mg orally daily.

arms.label: HER2-positive comparator
arms.text: Nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 and carboplatin AUC 1.5 on days 1, 8, and 21, plus trastuzumab and pertuzumab, for six 28-day cycles.

arms.label: HR-negative HER2-negative precision
arms.text: Immunomodulatory subtype: camrelizumab 200 mg intravenously every 2 weeks plus standard chemotherapy. Basal-like immune-suppressed subtype: fluzoparib 50 mg orally twice daily plus standard chemotherapy. HER2-low: SHR-A1811 4.8 mg/kg every 3 weeks for eight cycles. HER2-negative: SHR-A1921 3.0 mg/kg every 3 weeks for eight cycles.

NCT05582499.schema_source: The open-access FASCINATE-N design paper (2024) and the 2026 HR-positive results paper state the subtype randomization and the named neoadjuvant regimens.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Pragmatic phase II cohort-multiple randomized trial embedded in a prospective registry. It tests whether a focal high-dose-rate brachytherapy boost plus stereotactic radiotherapy reduces urinary decline compared with whole-gland high-dose-rate boost plus radiotherapy. Planned enrollment is 150.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Intermediate- or high-risk prostate cancer planned for curative high-dose-rate brachytherapy boost, with MRI and/or PSMA PET disease covering less than half of the prostate, ECOG 0-1, and Charlson comorbidity index at most 5.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Registry patients meeting eligibility are randomly selected 1:1 to be offered the experimental treatment. Patients not selected, and those who decline, receive standard whole-gland boost. Androgen deprivation follows standard care.

arms.label: Focal boost plus stereotactic radiotherapy
arms.text: Focal high-dose-rate brachytherapy, 13 to 15 Gy in one fraction to the gross tumor, then stereotactic radiotherapy 36.25 to 40 Gy in 5 fractions to the prostate every other day, with or without 25 Gy in 5 fractions to the elective pelvis.

arms.label: Whole-gland boost plus radiotherapy
arms.text: Whole-gland high-dose-rate brachytherapy, 15 Gy in one fraction, with or without an integrated gross-tumor dose of 18.75 Gy, followed within 14 days by external radiotherapy to an EQD2 of 43 to 47 Gy in 5 to 22 fractions, with or without elective pelvic radiotherapy.

NCT04100174.schema_source: Open-access fBTsRT protocol (BMC Cancer, 2022) states the cohort-multiple randomization and both brachytherapy-boost schedules.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Phase II trial of MRI-guided daily adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy for localized prostate cancer, randomizing men to two fractions with a tumor boost or to five fractions without a gross-tumor boost.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: A 3 mm margin expands each clinical target volume to the planning target volume. Each two-fraction treatment is delivered as two sequential sub-fractions.

arms.label: Two fractions with tumor boost
arms.text: 27 Gy to the MRI-visible gross tumor with no margin, 24 Gy to the prostate planning target volume, and 20 Gy to the seminal-vesicle planning target volume.

arms.label: Five fractions without gross-tumor boost
arms.text: 36.25 Gy to the prostate planning target volume and 30 Gy to the seminal-vesicle planning target volume. The prostate clinical target volume without a margin receives 40 Gy, as in PACE. There is no gross-tumor boost.

NCT04595019.schema_source: Open-access HERMES dosimetry paper (Cancers, 2024) states the randomization and the two-fraction and five-fraction prescriptions in the methods.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center open-label phase III trial comparing neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus surgery with CROSS-regimen neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy plus surgery for resectable locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint is overall survival. The sample size is 456 patients.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, age 18 to 70 years, ECOG 0-1, clinical stage cT2-T4a N+ M0 or cT3-4a N0 M0 (UICC 8th edition), no metastatic cervical nodes, and expected R0 resection.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: After eligibility is confirmed, sealed opaque envelopes assign patients 1:1. The protocol text does not list stratification factors.

arms.label: Arm A, chemotherapy then surgery
arms.text: Two cycles, every 3 weeks, of paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 and cisplatin 75 mg/m2 on day 1. Cisplatin may be divided over 3 days. Surgery follows.

arms.label: Arm B, CROSS chemoradiotherapy then surgery
arms.text: Weekly paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 and carboplatin AUC 2 for 5 cycles with concurrent radiotherapy, 41.4 Gy in 23 fractions over 5 weeks, then surgery.

NCT04138212.schema_source: Open-access HCHTOG1903 protocol (BMC Cancer, 2020) states the 1:1 assignment and both neoadjuvant regimens.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter open-label randomized phase III non-inferiority trial of one-week versus three-week adjuvant breast radiotherapy. The primary comparison is 5-year locoregional recurrence. The sample size is 2100 patients, accrued over 5 years.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Non-metastatic invasive breast cancer after mastectomy or breast conservation with clear margins. Breast conservation and neoadjuvant chemotherapy are eligible. Post-mastectomy eligibility is T3-T4, more than 3 positive nodes, or T0-T2 with 0-3 nodes and a Cambridge score of 3 or more. In situ disease, non-epithelial and metaplastic primaries, residual internal-mammary or supraclavicular nodes, prior breast radiotherapy, and concurrent chemotherapy are excluded.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Permuted-block randomization is stratified by mastectomy versus breast conservation, regional nodal radiotherapy required or not, triple-negative disease yes or no, and institution.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1 to the same breast or chest-wall volume, with or without regional nodes. A simultaneous integrated boost is allowed after breast conservation.

arms.label: Three-week radiotherapy
arms.text: 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks. The allowed simultaneous integrated boost is 8 Gy.

arms.label: One-week radiotherapy
arms.text: 26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week. The allowed simultaneous integrated boost is 6 Gy.

NCT03788213.schema_source: Open-access HYPORT-Adjuvant protocol (Trials, 2020) states the stratification factors, the 40 Gy and 26 Gy schedules, and the boost doses.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Open-label randomized phase III non-inferiority trial of 1 week versus 2 weeks of adjuvant whole-breast or chest-wall radiotherapy, with or without regional nodes, after surgery for breast cancer. The primary endpoint is locoregional control. The sample size is 1018 patients.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Age 18 to 75 years with invasive breast carcinoma after breast conservation or total mastectomy, with axillary staging or clearance and complete microscopic excision. Implant reconstruction is not allowed. Tissue expanders with distant metal ports are allowed. Concurrent trastuzumab and hormone therapy are allowed.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Simple 1:1 randomization without stratification. Allocation is not masked. Patients who change schedule are treated with 34 Gy in 10 fractions or 40 Gy in 15 fractions.

arms.label: One-week radiotherapy
arms.text: 26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week to the breast or chest wall and, when treated, axilla level III and the supraclavicular fossa. After breast conservation, a sequential boost of 8 Gy in 2 fractions or a simultaneous integrated boost to a total of 32 Gy.

arms.label: Two-week radiotherapy
arms.text: 34 Gy in 10 fractions over 2 weeks to the same volumes. After breast conservation, the boost total is 40 Gy.

NCT04472845.schema_source: Open-access HYPART protocol (Trials, 2024) states unstratified 1:1 randomization and the 26 Gy and 34 Gy schedules with boost totals.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Open-label multicenter randomized phase III non-inferiority trial of hypofractionated versus conventional IMRT when regional nodal irradiation, including internal mammary nodes, is indicated after breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy. The primary endpoint is 5-year locoregional recurrence.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Age 18 to 75 years with unilateral pT1-3 invasive breast cancer and histologically positive axillary nodes after breast conservation or mastectomy. Reconstruction is allowed. Adjuvant endocrine therapy and anti-HER2 therapy may continue during radiotherapy.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified by center, breast conservation versus mastectomy, and 1 to 3 versus 4 or more positive axillary nodes.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1. The dose covers the ipsilateral chest wall or whole breast and regional nodes. The dose-prescription section sets the hypofractionated dose at 40.05 Gy in 15 fractions.

arms.label: Hypofractionated IMRT
arms.text: 40.05 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks. After breast conservation, a sequential tumor-bed boost of 10.68 Gy in 4 fractions.

arms.label: Conventional IMRT
arms.text: 50 Gy in 25 fractions. After breast conservation, a sequential tumor-bed boost of 10 Gy in 5 fractions.

schema.note: The abstract also describes 2.67 Gy for 16 fractions. The methods dose-prescription section specifies 40.05 Gy in 15 fractions for enrolled patients.

NCT03829553.schema_source: Open-access HARVEST protocol (BMJ Open, 2022) states the stratification and, in the dose-prescription section, 40.05 Gy in 15 fractions versus 50 Gy in 25 fractions.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter open-label randomized phase III trial of intensity-modulated photon radiotherapy versus proton beam radiotherapy for glioblastoma. The primary endpoint is the cumulative rate of CTCAE grade 2 or higher toxicity in the first 4 months. The planned sample is 326 patients.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Adults with ECOG 0-2 and histologically confirmed glioblastoma who have an indication for radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Stratification factors are fractionation (normofractionated versus hypofractionated), subventricular-zone involvement (yes or no), and concurrent chemotherapy (yes or no).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1. The same prescribed dose is used in both arms. Concurrent or adjuvant chemotherapy and tumor-treating fields follow standard care outside the radiotherapy comparison.

arms.label: IMRT
arms.text: Photon IMRT, 30 fractions of 2 Gy or 33 fractions of 1.8 Gy. Patients treated with the hypofractionation protocol because of age or comorbidity receive 15 fractions of 2.67 Gy.

arms.label: Proton therapy
arms.text: Proton beam radiotherapy using the same three dose schedules, prescribed in Gy (RBE) to the planning target volume.

NCT04752280.schema_source: Open-access GRIPS protocol (Radiation Oncology, 2021) states the 1:1 randomization, three stratification factors, and shared dose schedules.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized phase III Proton Collaborative Group GU003 trial of moderately hypofractionated proton beam therapy with or without androgen suppression for intermediate-risk prostate adenocarcinoma. The primary endpoint is freedom from failure.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Intermediate-risk intact prostate cancer, ECOG 0-1, and International Prostate Symptom Score 16 or lower. MRI evidence of extracapsular extension or seminal-vesicle invasion, prior prostatectomy or pelvic radiotherapy, prior androgen suppression, and specified anticoagulation excluded patients.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomized to two arms. Both received the same proton dose to the prostate.

arms.label: Proton therapy alone
arms.text: 70 Gy relative biologic effectiveness in 28 daily fractions of 2.5 Gy, five days a week.

arms.label: Proton therapy plus androgen suppression
arms.text: The same 70 Gy in 28 fractions plus 6 months of androgen suppression.

NCT01492972.schema_source: Open-access GU003 quality-of-life report (Advances in Radiation Oncology, 2023) states the randomization and the 70 Gy proton schedule with or without 6 months of androgen suppression.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized open-label multicenter phase II trial of low-dose radiotherapy and stereotactic body radiotherapy added to sintilimab and chemotherapy for previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic squamous non-small-cell lung cancer, stage IIIB-IV, that is unresectable or unsuitable for radical chemoradiotherapy. The sample size is 114 patients.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified by PD-L1 tumor proportion score (below 1% versus 1% or higher) and by brain metastases (present versus absent).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1. In the experimental arm, radiotherapy is completed and sintilimab plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy starts within 1 week.

arms.label: Radiotherapy plus sintilimab and chemotherapy
arms.text: Stereotactic body radiotherapy 30 Gy in 3 fractions to the gross tumor and low-dose radiotherapy 4 Gy in 2 fractions to its planning target volume: 10 Gy to the gross tumor and 2 Gy to the low-dose volume on days 1 and 2, then 10 Gy to the gross tumor alone on day 3. Sintilimab plus four cycles of platinum-doublet chemotherapy follows, and sintilimab may continue for up to 24 months or 35 cycles.

arms.label: Sintilimab and chemotherapy
arms.text: Sintilimab plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy without protocol radiotherapy.

NCT06121505.schema_source: Open-access IHC002 protocol (BMJ Open, 2025) states the stratification and the 30 Gy and 4 Gy radiotherapy prescriptions with sintilimab.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm single-institution phase 2 trial of neoadjuvant genomic-adjusted, MRI-habitat-directed dose escalation for resectable non-metastatic high-grade soft-tissue sarcoma of the deep trunk or extremity. The primary endpoint is favorable pathologic response, defined as at least 95% treatment effect.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Adults with grade 2 or higher deep trunk or extremity sarcoma judged resectable before enrollment.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: There is no randomization. IMRT uses a simultaneous integrated boost in 25 fractions, with one planned adaptation from a multiparametric MRI at weeks 2 to 3. Surgery follows.

arms.label: Habitat-directed neoadjuvant radiotherapy
arms.text: 70 Gy to the highest-radioresistance habitat, 60 Gy to the intermediate habitat, and 50 Gy to the remaining volume, all in 25 fractions. Habitats are redrawn and doses adapted at the mid-treatment MRI.

NCT05301283.schema_source: Open-access HEAT protocol (BMC Cancer, 2024) states the single-arm 70 Gy, 60 Gy, and 50 Gy simultaneous integrated boost.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter randomized phase II trial testing whether stereotactic ablative radiotherapy to all liver metastases improves progression-free survival when added to first-line anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, with or without platinum chemotherapy, in metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer. The sample size is 68 patients.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Adults with newly diagnosed stage IV non-small-cell lung cancer involving the liver, without known EGFR, ALK, BRAF, or ROS1 alterations, ECOG 0-2, and liver metastases suitable for ablative radiotherapy. Patients may be enrolled up to the start of cycle 3 of immunotherapy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1. Liver radiotherapy should preferably finish before immunotherapy and must finish before cycle 3 or within 90 days of starting immunotherapy.

arms.label: Arm 1, systemic therapy
arms.text: Standard first-line anti-PD-(L)1 immunotherapy with or without platinum chemotherapy.

arms.label: Arm 2, systemic therapy plus liver SABR
arms.text: The same systemic therapy plus stereotactic ablative radiotherapy to every liver metastasis, 30 to 60 Gy in 3 to 6 fractions according to institutional standards and normal-liver dose.

NCT05657873.schema_source: Open-access HAMMER-NSCLC protocol (BMC Cancer, 2025) states the 1:1 randomization and the liver radiotherapy dose range.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective multicenter single-arm EMBRACE II study of image-guided intensity-modulated external-beam radiochemotherapy and MRI-based adaptive brachytherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer. It is not a randomized comparison.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Locally advanced cervical cancer suitable for curative radiochemotherapy and brachytherapy. Patients with para-aortic nodes up to L2 may be included. Further dissemination is excluded.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: All patients receive external-beam radiotherapy, concomitant chemotherapy, and image-guided adaptive brachytherapy. Overall treatment time, including brachytherapy, is at most 50 days.

arms.label: Chemoradiotherapy and adaptive brachytherapy
arms.text: IMRT or VMAT, 45 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks, with daily image guidance and a 5 mm PTV margin. Involved nodes receive a simultaneous integrated boost so that external-beam plus brachytherapy dose reaches 60 Gy EQD2. Weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 is standard unless precluded, with a goal of at least 5 cycles. MRI-guided adaptive brachytherapy follows protocol EQD2 planning aims, including a CTV-HR D90 planning aim above 90 Gy and a prescribed-dose limit above 85 Gy.

NCT03617133.schema_source: Open-access EMBRACE II methods paper (Clinical and Translational Radiation Oncology, 2018) states the single-arm external-beam dose, nodal boost, cisplatin schedule, and brachytherapy planning aims.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: NOA-18 / IMPROVE CODEL randomized trial for newly diagnosed CNS WHO grade 2 or 3 oligodendroglioma with 1p/19q codeletion. The primary endpoint is qualified overall survival, defined as overall survival without sustained functional, cognitive, or quality-of-life deterioration. Accrual is 182 patients per group.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized between initial radiotherapy followed by PCV and initial radiation-free CETEG chemotherapy with radiotherapy reserved for progression. Radiotherapy is partial-brain: 59.4 Gy in 33 fractions of 1.8 Gy for grade 3, and 50.4 or 54 Gy in 28 fractions of 1.8 Gy for grade 2.

arms.label: Radiotherapy then PCV
arms.text: Partial-brain radiotherapy followed by up to six 6-week cycles of PCV: lomustine 110 mg/m2 orally on day 1 (cap 200 mg), vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 intravenously on days 8 and 29 (cap 2 mg), and procarbazine 60 mg/m2 orally on days 8 to 21 (cap 100 mg). Treatment at later progression is best investigator choice.

arms.label: CETEG, radiotherapy at progression
arms.text: Six 6-week cycles of lomustine 100 mg/m2 orally on day 1 (cap 200 mg) and temozolomide 100 mg/m2 on days 2 to 6 of cycle 1, escalated by 50 mg/m2 steps as toxicity allows. At progression, radiotherapy plus PCV is used when marrow reserve and safety allow.

NCT05331521.schema_source: Open-access NOA-18 protocol (BMC Cancer, 2022) states the randomization, radiotherapy doses, and PCV and CETEG schedules.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Scandinavian Prostate Cancer Group 19 / GRand-P is a randomized multicenter phase III trial in Norway, Denmark, Finland, and Sweden. It compares immediate curative treatment with conservative treatment in older men with non-metastatic high-risk prostate cancer. Planned follow-up is 10 years. The primary endpoints are overall survival and health-related quality of life.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Men 75 years or older with non-metastatic high-risk prostate cancer are screened with the Geriatric 8 tool and Mini-COG. Participants scored fit or frail are eligible for randomization. Men who cannot or will not be randomized are enrolled in a separate observation group.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Fit or frail participants are randomized 1:1. The abstract does not state a radiotherapy dose or a drug name.

arms.label: Immediate curative therapy
arms.text: Radiotherapy or prostatectomy.

arms.label: Conservative therapy
arms.text: Endocrine therapy or observation.

NCT05448547.schema_source: The PubMed abstract of the SPCG 19/GRand-P protocol (BJU International, 2024) states the 1:1 randomization to radiotherapy or prostatectomy versus endocrine therapy or observation. The full text is paywalled and was not used.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: NSMP-ORANGE is the randomized phase III de-escalation trial within the RAINBO platform for estrogen-receptor-positive endometrial cancer with no specific molecular profile. It is led from the United Kingdom. The platform paper does not apply blinding.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Estrogen-receptor-positive stage II disease with lymphovascular space invasion, or stage III disease, with no specific molecular profile.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: A minimization algorithm balances center, stage, and lymphadenectomy or sentinel-node biopsy, and includes a random element.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized to radiotherapy followed by progestin or to adjuvant chemoradiation.

arms.label: Radiotherapy then progestin
arms.text: Adjuvant radiotherapy followed by progesterone tablets, either medroxyprogesterone acetate or megestrol acetate, for 2 years.

arms.label: Adjuvant chemoradiation
arms.text: Adjuvant chemoradiation alone. The platform paper does not state the external-beam dose or chemotherapy drugs for this arm.

protocol:EN12 (RAINBO ORANGE).schema_source: Open-access RAINBO program paper (International Journal of Gynecological Cancer, 2023) states the NSMP-ORANGE randomization, stratification, and progestin versus chemoradiation comparison.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Pragmatic open-label multicenter randomized phase III non-inferiority trial for operable locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint is overall survival. The target is 1200 randomized patients. The experimental arm is also tested for superior global quality of life at 1 year.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Histologically confirmed esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, cT1 N+ or cT2-4a any N, M0, technically resectable, age 18 to 80 years, and ECOG 0-1.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Minimization stratifies by sex, age under 70 versus 70 or older, upper versus middle versus lower esophageal third, ECOG 0 versus 1, clinical node status, clinical T4a versus any other T, and center.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Eligible patients are randomized 1:1 before any antitumor treatment.

arms.label: Arm A, neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and planned surgery
arms.text: Carboplatin AUC 2 and paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 weekly for 5 weeks with radiotherapy 41.4 Gy in 23 fractions of 1.8 Gy, then esophagectomy within 8 weeks, matching the CROSS intervention.

arms.label: Arm B, definitive chemoradiotherapy and salvage surgery if needed
arms.text: Radiotherapy 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions of 1.8 Gy or 50 Gy in 25 fractions of 2 Gy, with weekly carboplatin AUC 2 plus paclitaxel 50 mg/m2, or cisplatin plus fluorouracil, or FOLFOX. Surveillance follows, and esophagectomy is used only for residual or recurrent locoregional cancer. No induction or adjuvant chemotherapy.

protocol:ES3 (NEEDS).schema_source: Open-access NEEDS protocol (Frontiers in Oncology, 2022) states the minimization factors and the CROSS neoadjuvant arm versus definitive chemoradiotherapy with selective salvage surgery.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Operable locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Randomization is before any antitumor treatment. Target accrual 1200.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Minimization by gender, age (under 70 versus 70 or older), tumor site (upper, middle, or lower third), ECOG 0 versus 1, clinical nodal status (positive versus negative or unknown), clinical T status (T4a versus any other T), and center.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Open-label phase III, 1:1. The primary comparison is overall survival, with a superiority hypothesis for quality of life after definitive chemoradiotherapy.

arms.label: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and planned surgery
arms.text: CROSS-like treatment: weekly carboplatin AUC 2 and paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 with 1.8 Gy x 23 (41.4 Gy), followed by planned esophagectomy.

arms.label: Definitive chemoradiotherapy and salvage surgery if needed
arms.text: 1.8 Gy x 28 (50.4 Gy) or 2.0 Gy x 25 (50 Gy), with weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel, cisplatin plus 5-fluorouracil, or FOLFOX. Surveillance follows, and esophagectomy is used only for residual or recurrent locoregional cancer.

NCT04460352.schema_source: The open-access NEEDS protocol states the 1:1 randomization, stratification factors, and the neoadjuvant versus definitive chemoradiotherapy doses and regimens.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: PORT-N1, designated KROG 22-05, is a prospective multicenter randomized phase 3 non-inferiority trial of postoperative radiotherapy de-escalation for pN1 breast cancer. The primary comparison is 7-year disease-free survival. The target is 1106 patients.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Women with pT1-3 N1 breast cancer after breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy. After mastectomy, at least 5 nodes must be dissected when one node is positive, and an axillary dissection is required when two or three nodes are positive.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified by breast-conserving surgery versus mastectomy and by triple-negative versus non-triple-negative histology.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1. Both hypofractionation and standard fractionation are allowed. Hypofractionation is 2.5 to 3.0 Gy per fraction, 39 to 45.9 Gy to the breast or chest wall, in 13 to 17 fractions. Standard fractionation is 1.8 to 2.0 Gy per fraction, 45 to 50.4 Gy, in 23 to 28 fractions. Tumor-bed boost dose is not restricted.

arms.label: Control, comprehensive postoperative radiotherapy
arms.text: After breast conservation, whole-breast irradiation plus regional nodes, using a high tangent or a wider field. Supraclavicular and internal mammary irradiation is permitted. After mastectomy, chest-wall irradiation with or without regional nodes.

arms.label: Experimental, de-escalated radiotherapy
arms.text: After breast conservation, whole-breast irradiation without regional nodal irradiation. After mastectomy, no radiotherapy.

protocol:KROG 22-05.schema_source: Open-access PORT-N1 protocol (BMC Cancer, 2022) identifies the trial as KROG 22-05 and states the stratified randomization and the control versus de-escalated volumes.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Women with pT1-3 N1 breast cancer after breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy, without neoadjuvant chemotherapy. After mastectomy, at least 5 nodes are dissected for one positive node, and axillary dissection is required for two or three positive nodes. Target accrual 1106.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Surgery type (breast-conserving surgery versus mastectomy) and histology (triple-negative versus non-triple-negative).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Phase III non-inferiority, 1:1. Regional nodal irradiation uses a high-tangent or wider field.

arms.label: Standard postoperative radiotherapy
arms.text: After breast-conserving surgery, whole-breast irradiation plus regional nodal irradiation. After mastectomy, post-mastectomy radiotherapy.

arms.label: De-escalated postoperative radiotherapy
arms.text: After breast-conserving surgery, whole-breast irradiation alone. After mastectomy, no post-mastectomy radiotherapy.

NCT05440149.schema_source: The open-access PORT-N1 protocol states the 1:1 randomization, the de-escalated versus standard postoperative radiotherapy comparison, and the stratification factors.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Phase III randomized trial comparing two planning techniques for the same accelerated partial breast irradiation dose. Primary comparisons were patient-reported pain and cosmesis.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Age at least 40 years, pathologic T0-T2 N0 breast cancer with invasive or DCIS span under 3 cm and margins at least 2 mm. ER-negative, PR-negative, and HER2-positive tumors were allowed. Gross multifocal disease was excluded.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: The protocol used no stratification factors. Randomization used a biased-coin method, with blocks of 30 if the arms became unequal.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomized to intensity-modulated or three-dimensional conformal accelerated partial breast irradiation. Both arms received 38.5 Gy in 10 twice-daily fractions of 3.85 Gy.

arms.label: IMRT
arms.text: Sliding-window or step-and-shoot IMRT. At least 95% of the CTV and PTV received at least 95% of 38.5 Gy.

arms.label: 3D-CRT
arms.text: At least four fields, wedges or forward-planned field-in-field allowed, with customized blocking around the PTV plus 0.5 cm for penumbra.

NCT01185132.schema_source: The phase III results paper states that patients were randomized, without stratification, to IMRT or 3D-CRT APBI at 38.5 Gy in 10 twice-daily fractions.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Proton Collaborative Group BRE007-12 is a multicenter single-arm phase II trial of proton partial breast irradiation after breast-conserving surgery. There is no randomization.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Women at least 50 years old with ER-positive, node-negative invasive ductal carcinoma or DCIS 3 cm or smaller and margins at least 2 mm. Lobular histology, lymphovascular invasion, BRCA1/2 mutation, and prior ipsilateral breast or thorax radiotherapy were excluded.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: All patients received the same proton partial breast prescription.

arms.label: Proton PBI
arms.text: 40 Gy (RBE) in 10 daily fractions of 4 Gy (RBE) over 2 weeks. Passive scattering used at least 3 fields; active scanning could use fewer fields if maximum skin dose was at most 100% of prescription. At least 95% of the PTV received 100% of prescription.

NCT01766297.schema_source: The open-access 3-year PCG BRE007-12 report states the single-arm proton partial breast dose of 40 Gy (RBE) in 10 daily fractions.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: International open-label phase 3 FORUM trial of conditioning before allogeneic transplant for pediatric high-risk or relapsed acute lymphoblastic leukemia in complete remission.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: High-risk or relapsed ALL, age 18 years or younger at diagnosis and 4 to 21 years at transplant, in complete remission, with an HLA-matched sibling or matched unrelated donor. The reported randomized comparison included 417 patients aged 4 to 18 years.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Eligible patients were randomized to total-body irradiation plus etoposide or to chemotherapy conditioning. The protocol chemotherapy backbones were fludarabine and thiotepa with either busulfan or treosulfan. In nonrandomizing countries the chemotherapy choice was set nationally.

arms.label: TBI plus etoposide
arms.text: Total-body irradiation plus etoposide. This paper does not restate the TBI dose or fraction number.

arms.label: Fludarabine, thiotepa, busulfan
arms.text: Fludarabine 30 mg/m2 daily for 5 days (150 mg/m2), thiotepa 5 mg/kg twice in 1 day (10 mg/kg), and busulfan over 4 days.

arms.label: Fludarabine, thiotepa, treosulfan
arms.text: The same fludarabine and thiotepa doses with treosulfan 14 g/m2 daily for 3 days (42 g/m2).

NCT01949129.schema_source: An open-access FORUM analysis states the randomized TBI-plus-etoposide versus fludarabine-thiotepa-busulfan or treosulfan conditioning comparison.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-group open-label phase 2 trial of preoperative ultrahypofractionated radiotherapy for extremity or trunk soft-tissue sarcoma, with an initial cohort and an expansion cohort. It is not randomized.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Age at least 18 years, ECOG 0-2, histologically confirmed extremity or trunk sarcoma recommended for preoperative radiotherapy and surgery, without distant metastases or prior radiotherapy to the primary. Concurrent chemotherapy was not allowed. The expansion cohort could enroll patients planned for neoadjuvant chemotherapy, but those patients were excluded from the reported analysis.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: All analyzed patients received the same preoperative dose, then surgery.

arms.label: Preoperative 5-fraction RT
arms.text: 30 Gy in 5 fractions of 6 Gy on consecutive weekdays to at least 95% of the PTV, followed by surgery within 12 weeks. CTV followed RTOG 0630: 3 cm longitudinal and 1.5 cm radial, edited for anatomy, plus a 5 mm PTV margin. IMRT was preferred.

NCT02701153.schema_source: The open-access trial report states that preoperative radiotherapy was 30 Gy in 5 fractions using RTOG 0630 volumes.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter single-arm phase 2 trial of second-line pembrolizumab plus GVD for transplant-eligible relapsed or refractory classic Hodgkin lymphoma. There is no randomized comparator.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Transplant-eligible relapsed or refractory classic Hodgkin lymphoma. In the reported cohort, 41% had primary refractory disease and 38% had relapsed within 1 year of first-line treatment.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: All patients received the same chemoimmunotherapy, then planned high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem-cell rescue.

arms.label: Pembrolizumab-GVD
arms.text: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV on day 1, gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8, vinorelbine 20 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8, and liposomal doxorubicin 15 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8, in 21-day cycles, for up to 4 cycles, followed by high-dose chemotherapy and autologous transplant.

NCT03618550.schema_source: The 5-year update abstract states the pembrolizumab-GVD doses, schedule, and planned autologous transplant.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: One-arm multicenter prospective trial of modular salvage chemoradiation for thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after esophagectomy. Patients are assigned, not randomized, to elective nodal irradiation or involved-field irradiation.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: R1 or R2 resection, locoregional recurrence after radical surgery, out-of-field recurrence after adjuvant radiotherapy, or recurrence after adjuvant chemotherapy. Age 16-70 years, KPS at least 70, no distant metastasis, and no prior therapy for the recurrence.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Assignment uses, in steps, R0 versus R1/R2 surgery, recurrent-lesion diameter, involved regions, and time to recurrence. Dose and technique are then modified by distance from the lesion to the thoracic stomach or intestine.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Two volume strategies, both with concurrent chemotherapy: paclitaxel 135-150 mg/m2 on day 1 plus lobaplatin or nedaplatin every 3 weeks for two cycles. Optional consolidation uses the same regimen.

arms.label: Elective nodal irradiation
arms.text: Prophylactic high-risk nodal CTV. For a lesion far from the thoracic stomach, the published SIB-IMRT example is PTV 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions and PGTV 59.92-62.16 Gy in 28 fractions. SIB versus sequential boost is chosen for stomach or bowel safety. If thoracic-stomach V50 exceeds 50%, the total dose is reduced to 45 Gy in 25 fractions.

arms.label: Involved-field irradiation
arms.text: CTV is GTV plus 0.6-0.8 cm radially and 1.0-1.5 cm craniocaudally, with no elective nodes. Away from stomach: 60 Gy in 30 fractions. Close to stomach: 59.4-61.2 Gy in 33-34 fractions. The same V50 stomach reduction to 45 Gy in 25 fractions applies.

schema.note: Not a randomized comparison. The exact decision tree is in the protocol figure.

NCT03731442.schema_source: The open-access protocol states stepwise assignment to elective nodal or involved-field salvage chemoradiation and gives the dose schedules.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Phase 2 study of neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade for mismatch-repair-deficient solid tumors amenable to curative-intent treatment. Two cohorts receive the same drug schedule. It is not a randomized treatment comparison.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Newly diagnosed stage I, II, or III solid tumors with loss of MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, or PMS2 and amenable to curative-intent therapy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both cohorts receive neoadjuvant dostarlimab. A clinical complete response may be managed without surgery. Residual disease proceeds to standard neoadjuvant therapy and surgery when applicable.

arms.label: Cohort 1, rectal
arms.text: Locally advanced mismatch-repair-deficient rectal cancer: dostarlimab 500 mg IV every 3 weeks for 9 cycles.

arms.label: Cohort 2, non-rectal
arms.text: Other stage I-III mismatch-repair-deficient solid tumors: the same dostarlimab schedule.

schema.note: Cohorts are disease groups, not randomized arms.

NCT04165772.schema_source: The open-access trial report states neoadjuvant dostarlimab 500 mg every 3 weeks for 9 cycles, with nonoperative management after a clinical complete response.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: ACCO is a prospective open-label randomized two-arm phase II trial at Heidelberg comparing carbon-ion radiotherapy alone with bimodal photon plus carbon-ion radiotherapy for node-negative head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma. Primary endpoint is locoregional control.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Node-negative adenoid cystic carcinoma of the head and neck, treated after recovery from resection or when inoperable. Active medical implants without ion-beam authorization are excluded.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified for residual tumor and lung metastases, in balanced permuted blocks.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 314 patients are assigned to carbon ions alone or bimodal treatment. Target doses refer to 95% of the volume. Carbon-ion biological dose uses LEM1 and an alpha/beta of 2 Gy.

arms.label: Carbon ion alone
arms.text: 51 Gy (RBE) in 17 fractions to the basic volume plus 15 Gy (RBE) in 5 fractions to the boost.

arms.label: Bimodal
arms.text: 50 Gy photon IMRT in 25 fractions plus a carbon-ion boost of 24 Gy (RBE) in 8 fractions of 3 Gy (RBE).

NCT04214366.schema_source: The open-access ACCO protocol states the stratified randomization and both radiotherapy dose schedules.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center single-cohort phase II trial of treatment intensification for molecular glioblastoma, meaning IDH-wildtype glioma that would historically have been WHO grade 2 or 3. It is not randomized.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Age at least 18 years, KPS at least 70, and a candidate for radiotherapy. Multicentric disease, prior brain radiotherapy or chemotherapy, metastatic disease, and leptomeningeal disease were excluded.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: All patients received the protocol radiotherapy, with concurrent and adjuvant chemotherapy allowed.

arms.label: 60 Gy with reduced CTV
arms.text: GTV includes cavity, contrast enhancement, and FLAIR tumor. CTV expansion is 1-2 cm, 1 cm from FLAIR for predominantly non-enhancing tumor, edited at anatomic boundaries. CTV dose is 50 Gy in 30 fractions with a simultaneous integrated boost; the prescription dose received was 60 Gy. Concurrent and adjuvant temozolomide was permitted.

NCT04623931.schema_source: The open-access phase II report states 60 Gy to gross disease, 50 Gy in 30 fractions to a 1-2 cm CTV, with chemotherapy allowed.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center phase 2, 1:1 randomized, investigator-blinded, non-inferiority trial of hypofractionated versus standard definitive chemoradiotherapy for uterine cervix cancer.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Biopsy-proven squamous, adeno, or adenosquamous cervix cancer, FIGO 2018 IIA to IIIC1, age 18-85, eligible for cisplatin, ECOG 0-2.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Permuted blocks of 6, stratified by FIGO stage.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both arms receive external-beam radiotherapy, weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2, a node boost for stage IIIC1, and brachytherapy 28 Gy in 4 weekly fractions starting 1 week after external-beam radiotherapy. The reported interim cohort used 3D conformal radiotherapy.

arms.label: Hypofractionated
arms.text: 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks with 3 weekly cisplatin doses. Stage IIIC1 receives an additional 8 Gy in 3 fractions to gross nodes.

arms.label: Standard
arms.text: 45 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks with up to 5 weekly cisplatin doses. Stage IIIC1 receives an additional 9 Gy in 5 fractions to gross nodes.

NCT04831437.schema_source: The open-access interim report states the stage-stratified randomization, external-beam doses, cisplatin schedule, node boosts, and brachytherapy.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Double-blind randomized phase II trial of brain-directed stereotactic radiation with or without AGuIX nanoparticles for brain metastases at higher risk of local recurrence after radiation alone.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Adults with brain metastases treated on Dana-Farber protocol 20-240. The imaging report does not restate the full eligibility list.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients receive AGuIX or saline placebo with protocol stereotactic radiation. Fractionation is a protocol option, not a separate randomized arm. The paper does not state the allocation ratio or stratification factors.

arms.label: AGuIX plus SRS or SRT
arms.text: AGuIX 100 mg/kg IV, with a 1-5 hour uptake interval (2 hours preferred), plus SRS 18-20 Gy in 1 fraction or SRT 30 Gy in 5 fractions or 25 Gy in 5 fractions.

arms.label: Placebo plus SRS or SRT
arms.text: Saline placebo on the same infusion schedule, with the same SRS or SRT dose options.

NCT04899908.schema_source: An open-access methods paper from the trial states double-blind AGuIX 100 mg/kg versus saline placebo and the stereotactic dose options.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: ReACT 1.0 is a non-randomized open-label phase 2 trial. Treatment intensity is assigned from clinical risk and on-treatment TTMV-HPV DNA clearance, not by randomization.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Age at least 22, HPV16-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma, AJCC 8th edition stage I-III, detectable pretreatment TTMV-HPV DNA, ECOG 0-2, planned for non-surgical curative treatment. Undetectable baseline score, non-HPV16 genotype, N3 disease, and fixed nodes were excluded.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Low risk is clinical T0-3 N0-2 with at most 10 pack-years and any detectable score. Intermediate risk is T4 or more than 10 pack-years with a baseline score above 200. Intermediate-risk patients with a baseline score of 200 or less were not eligible for de-escalation. Intermediate-risk patients who clear more than 95% of HPV DNA by mid-treatment are reclassified to the low-risk plan.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Assigned radiotherapy and chemotherapy depend on the risk group.

arms.label: De-escalated
arms.text: IMRT 54-60 Gy in 30 fractions to primary and gross nodes. Elective volumes 30-54 Gy, with 48 Gy in 30 fractions preferred. Radiation alone at 54-66 Gy was allowed for T0-2 N0-1. Preferred cisplatin total at most 200 mg/m2, or weekly carboplatin AUC 1.5 plus paclitaxel 45 mg/m2 if cisplatin-ineligible.

arms.label: Standard if no clearance
arms.text: 70 Gy in 35 fractions, elective dose 56-63 Gy, with cisplatin up to 300 mg/m2 or 7 weeks of weekly carboplatin plus paclitaxel.

schema.note: Assignment rules, not randomized arms.

NCT04900623.schema_source: The open-access ReACT 1.0 report states the HPV-DNA risk groups and the de-escalated versus 70 Gy chemoradiation schedules.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: CERVANTES is an international multicenter randomized phase III non-inferiority trial. Primary endpoint is disease-free survival. Planned sample size is 514.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Intermediate-risk early-stage cervical cancer, FIGO IB1-IIA, node-negative, after radical surgery. Intermediate risk is a combination of tumor size greater than 4 cm, tumor size greater than 2 cm with lymphovascular invasion, or deep stromal invasion greater than two thirds. The abstract also lists a tumor-free distance factor, but the numeric cutoff is truncated in the available abstract.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1 after radical surgery. Radiotherapy dose and chemotherapy drugs are not specified in the abstract.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: No additional treatment after radical surgery.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Adjuvant external-beam radiotherapy with or without brachytherapy and with or without concomitant chemotherapy.

NCT04989647.schema_source: The CERVANTES trial-design abstract states 1:1 randomization to observation versus adjuvant external-beam radiotherapy with or without brachytherapy and chemotherapy.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: NOTABLE-306 has a phase Ib 3+3 dose-escalation stage to choose the nimotuzumab dose, then a phase III randomized double-blind placebo-controlled stage. The phase III primary endpoint is progression-free survival.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Treatment-naive women aged 18-80 with cervical squamous carcinoma, FIGO 2018 IB3 to IVA, and no prior definitive treatment.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Phase III randomizes 1:1 to nimotuzumab or placebo, weekly for 8 cycles, then every 2 weeks for 24 weeks of maintenance. All patients receive the same chemoradiotherapy. The selected nimotuzumab milligram dose is not stated in the protocol summary.

arms.label: Nimotuzumab plus chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: Weekly nimotuzumab for 8 cycles, then biweekly maintenance for 24 weeks, with pelvic IMRT or VMAT 45-50 Gy in 25 fractions, simultaneous or sequential boost to 60-65 Gy for involved nodes or invaded parametrium, high-dose-rate brachytherapy 30-40 Gy, cumulative high-risk CTV D90 80-85 Gy (at least 87 Gy if tumor diameter exceeds 4 cm), and weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 for 4-5 cycles.

arms.label: Placebo plus chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: The same radiotherapy, brachytherapy, cisplatin, and maintenance schedule, with placebo instead of nimotuzumab.

NCT06333821.schema_source: The open-access NOTABLE-306 protocol states the 1:1 nimotuzumab versus placebo randomization and the chemoradiotherapy dose ranges.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase 2 trial of durvalumab added to chemoradiotherapy for limited-stage small-cell lung cancer. There is no randomized comparator.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Adults with newly diagnosed limited-stage small-cell lung cancer, ECOG 0-1, and at least one measurable lesion. Prior antitumor therapy was excluded.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: All patients receive durvalumab with platinum-etoposide and thoracic radiotherapy, then durvalumab alone.

arms.label: Durvalumab plus chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: Durvalumab 10 mg/kg every 3 weeks with etoposide plus cisplatin or carboplatin. Thoracic radiotherapy is 60 Gy to gross tumor and 54 Gy to the planning target volume in 30 once-daily fractions, given with chemoimmunotherapy. Durvalumab then continues every 3 weeks for at least 1 year. Prophylactic cranial irradiation is recommended after a complete or partial response.

schema.note: The paper reports variable induction length, so a fixed induction cycle count is not stated as a protocol rule.

NCT06371482.schema_source: The open-access single-arm trial report states durvalumab 10 mg/kg every 3 weeks, thoracic doses of 60 Gy and 54 Gy in 30 fractions, and consolidation durvalumab.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: CBART is a prospective single-arm phase II trial of central-boost ablative stereotactic radiotherapy for large tumors or tumors next to the gastrointestinal tract. There is no randomization.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients with large solid tumors or tumors adjacent to the gastrointestinal tract who are treated with this stereotactic technique. The protocol summary does not limit enrollment to one histology.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Every patient receives CBART, then sequential systemic therapy chosen by histology and stage.

arms.label: Central-boost SBRT
arms.text: GTV is radiographically evident disease. The central core is contracted so its volume is 50% of the GTV and has no added margin. PTV is GTV plus 2-5 mm. Margin prescription is 30-45 Gy in 5 fractions, set by site and histology. Central-core prescription is 120-150% of the margin dose. Ninety percent of the PTV and central core are covered. Delivery described with CyberKnife.

NCT06427460.schema_source: The open-access CBART protocol states the single-arm 5-fraction margin dose and the 120-150% central boost.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: AUSTRAL is an open-label multicenter single-arm phase II trial. There is no randomization. Planned enrollment is 21 patients.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Stage III non-small-cell lung cancer with locoregional relapse more than 12 months after chemoradiotherapy, with or without up to 3 metastatic lesions, after a PACIFIC or PACIFIC-like durvalumab regimen.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: All patients receive local radiotherapy followed by durvalumab plus ceralasertib.

arms.label: Radiotherapy then durvalumab and ceralasertib
arms.text: Thoracic irradiation, with stereotactic body radiotherapy to oligometastases when used, followed 2 to 4 weeks later by durvalumab plus ceralasertib until progression or severe toxicity.

schema.note: Single-arm assignment. Drug doses were not stated in the design abstract.

NCT06680050.schema_source: The AUSTRAL design abstract states the single-arm sequence of thoracic radiotherapy with or without metastasis-directed SBRT, then durvalumab plus ceralasertib.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: TRIUMPH-B01 is a phase II randomized, non-comparative, open-label multicenter trial of two bladder-preservation strategies. Planned enrollment is 80 patients. Primary endpoint is the 2-year proportion with the bladder preserved.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Muscle-invasive urothelial bladder cancer, T2-T4N0M0.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1. Both arms start with the same induction. Radiotherapy is given only after a complete or near-complete response. Non-responders are referred for salvage cystectomy. The abstract does not state stratification factors.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Induction dose-dense MVAC or gemcitabine-cisplatin plus avelumab, restaging with imaging and TURBT, then 55 Gy in 20 fractions if response is complete or near-complete, followed by maintenance avelumab for 1 year.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: The same induction, response assessment, and 55 Gy in 20 fractions, then watch and wait without maintenance avelumab.

NCT06686381.schema_source: The TRIUMPH-B01 design abstract states 1:1 randomization, shared induction and 55 Gy in 20 fractions, then avelumab maintenance versus observation.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center single-arm phase II trial using a Simon two-stage design. There is no randomization. Planned enrollment is 27 patients.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Driver-gene-negative advanced non-small-cell lung cancer with bone metastases and no prior systemic therapy. Small-cell and mixed small-cell histology are excluded.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: All patients receive narlumosbart, bone stereotactic radiotherapy, and then first-line chemoimmunotherapy.

arms.label: Narlumosbart, bone SBRT, then chemoimmunotherapy
arms.text: Narlumosbart 120 mg subcutaneously every 4 weeks. Bone SBRT is 24 Gy in 3 fractions for spine and 30-35 Gy in 5 fractions for non-spine lesions, given 3 days before chemoimmunotherapy. The radiation oncologist may adjust the radiotherapy regimen. First-line chemotherapy plus immunotherapy follows guideline therapy.

NCT06738160.schema_source: The open-access protocol states narlumosbart 120 mg every 4 weeks, the bone SBRT doses, and subsequent first-line chemoimmunotherapy.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: BREAST is a prospective single-arm phase II trial of partial-breast proton reirradiation after repeat breast-conserving surgery. Planned enrollment is 20 patients. There is no randomization.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Histologically proven ipsilateral invasive breast-cancer recurrence after repeat breast-conserving surgery, with an indication for local reirradiation and at least 1 year since prior radiotherapy to that breast.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: All patients receive the same proton partial-breast reirradiation.

arms.label: Proton partial-breast reirradiation
arms.text: 40.05 Gy (RBE) in 15 once-daily fractions of 2.67 Gy (RBE), 5 fractions per week, with active raster-scanning protons and a fixed RBE of 1.1. The evaluated PTV should receive 95-107% of prescription.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: BITS-TO-HCC is a prospective single-center single-arm phase II trial. Planned enrollment is 54 patients. There is no randomization. Primary endpoint is progression-free survival.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Unresectable BCLC stage C hepatocellular carcinoma with portal-vein tumor thrombus and/or extrahepatic oligometastases, Child-Pugh A, ECOG 0-1. Intended stereotactic targets must meet protocol liver and organ-at-risk constraints in a 5-fraction plan.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: All patients receive hepatic-artery infusion chemotherapy and systemic therapy, then stereotactic radiotherapy if disease has not progressed and a suitable target remains.

arms.label: HAIC-FO, bispecific antibody, bevacizumab, then SBRT
arms.text: Up to four cycles of HAIC-FO: oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2, leucovorin 200 mg/m2, fluorouracil 400 mg/m2 bolus, then fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 hours. After hepatic laboratory reassessment, bevacizumab 15 mg/kg and iparomlimab/tuvonralimab 7.5 mg/kg. After cycle 4, patients without progression receive 25-40 Gy in 5 fractions to residual SBRT-amenable disease, including portal-vein thrombus or oligometastases. Complete response or no SBRT target continues systemic therapy.

schema.note: Single-arm assignment. The first six patients are a safety cohort.

NCT07062055.schema_source: The open-access BITS-TO-HCC protocol states the single-arm HAIC-FO, bevacizumab, iparomlimab/tuvonralimab, and 25-40 Gy in 5 fraction sequence.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Resectable locally recurrent rectal cancer after prior partial or total mesorectal excision, without synchronous distant metastases or recent chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Target accrual 364.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Phase III, 1:1. Experimental treatment is induction chemotherapy, then chemoradiotherapy and surgery. Control treatment is chemoradiotherapy and surgery. In the experimental arm, stable or responding disease gets one more CAPOX cycle or two more FOLFOX or FOLFIRI cycles before chemoradiotherapy.

arms.label: Induction then chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: Three 3-week cycles of CAPOX, or four 2-week cycles of FOLFOX or FOLFIRI, then chemoradiotherapy and surgery. Radiotherapy-naive patients receive 25 x 2.0 Gy or 28 x 1.8 Gy. Previously irradiated patients receive 15 x 2.0 Gy. Capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily is given on radiotherapy days.

arms.label: Chemoradiotherapy alone
arms.text: The same chemoradiotherapy schedule and capecitabine, then surgery, without induction chemotherapy.

schema.text: Phase II, two arms. Fractionation is chosen within allowed schemes rather than assigned by the randomization.

arms.text: CTV_high is GTV plus 5 mm inside the prostate. CTV_low is the remaining prostate, with seminal vesicles optional, at a lower dose. Pelvic nodes are optional. Experimental doses, as GTV D98 / CTV_high / CTV_low / nodes: 39-40 fractions, up to 94 Gy / 78-80 Gy / 56 Gy in 28 / 50.4 Gy in 28; 28 fractions, up to 84 / 70 / 56 / 50.4 Gy; 20 fractions, up to 74 / 60 / 56 / 44 Gy; 5-fraction SBRT, up to 45 / 40 / 30 / 25 Gy.

arms.label: Standard whole-gland dose
arms.text: The whole prostate receives the CTV_high prescription for the chosen fractionation: 78-80 Gy in 39-40 fractions, 70 Gy in 28, 60 Gy in 20, or 40 Gy in 5. A focal boost to MRI-visible disease is allowed but not required.

schema.label: Entry

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective multicenter single-arm phase 2 trial for newly diagnosed EBV-positive nasopharyngeal carcinoma in children and adults. Patients are allocated, not randomized, by age, induction response, and metastases. Induction for non-metastatic disease is three cycles of cisplatin 100 mg/m2 over 6 hours and 5-fluorouracil 1000 mg/m2/day for 5 days, with nivolumab 4.5 mg/kg (maximum 360 mg) every 3 weeks.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Radiotherapy and concurrent chemotherapy then follow one of five protocol pathways.

arms.label: Age 25 or younger, non-metastatic, complete or partial response
arms.text: Nivolumab stops after three induction doses. Partial response: 45.0 Gy to the elective volume and a boost to 59.4 Gy at 1.8 Gy per fraction. Complete response: boost reduced so total dose is 54.0 Gy. Concurrent cisplatin 20 mg/m2 on days 1-3 of the first and last radiotherapy week, then interferon-beta maintenance.

arms.label: Age 25 or younger, stable or progressive disease, or initial metastases
arms.text: Nivolumab continues through chemoradiotherapy for six doses, or seven if metastatic disease responds and a fourth chemotherapy cycle is given. Chemoradiotherapy uses the same dose rules as the responding non-metastatic group.

arms.label: Age older than 25, non-metastatic, complete or partial response
arms.text: Same three-cycle induction. Radiotherapy 66-70.2 Gy by adult guidelines. Concurrent cisplatin totaling 200-300 mg/m2 by local practice. No interferon maintenance.

arms.label: Age older than 25, stable or progressive disease, or initial metastases
arms.text: Non-response uses the adult chemoradiotherapy doses with nivolumab continued for six doses. Initial metastases use three cycles of gemcitabine and cisplatin, nivolumab through chemoradiotherapy, and irradiation of metastases according to published guidelines. A fourth cycle and a seventh nivolumab dose are allowed after response.
