schema.text: Patients were randomized to nivolumab plus AVD or brentuximab vedotin plus AVD.

arms.label: Nivolumab plus AVD
arms.text: Nivolumab plus doxorubicin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine.

arms.label: Brentuximab vedotin plus AVD
arms.text: Brentuximab vedotin plus doxorubicin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine.

schema.note: This report is the HIV-associated subset and restates the parent trial arms. It does not describe radiotherapy as a randomized arm.

NCT03907488.schema_source: PubMed abstract of the S1826 HIV-associated report states the nivolumab plus AVD versus brentuximab plus AVD randomization (PMID 42577949).

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma of any histology with at least one bone metastasis (Alliance A031801, RADICAL).

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Osteoclast-targeted therapy, prior therapy, opioid use, and International mRCC Database Consortium risk.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to cabozantinib with or without radium-223.

arms.label: Cabozantinib plus radium-223
arms.text: Cabozantinib plus radium-223 dichloride.

arms.label: Cabozantinib
arms.text: Cabozantinib without radium-223.

schema.note: The abstract does not restate cabozantinib or radium-223 dose. Planned target 124 evaluable patients.

NCT04071223.schema_source: PubMed abstract of Alliance A031801 states the 1:1 assignment and stratification factors (PMID 42507969).

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: T1-T3 N0 M0 non-small-cell lung cancer 7 cm or smaller, medically inoperable or surgery declined, with at least one recurrence risk factor (SWOG/NRG S1914).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients underwent equal stratified randomization to stereotactic body radiotherapy with or without atezolizumab.

arms.label: SBRT plus atezolizumab
arms.text: Stereotactic body radiotherapy over 3 to 8 fractions, plus atezolizumab 1200 mg intravenously every 21 days for up to eight cycles, with radiotherapy started at cycle 3.

arms.label: SBRT
arms.text: Stereotactic body radiotherapy alone over 3 to 8 fractions.

schema.note: 417 patients were assigned (210 atezolizumab plus SBRT, 207 SBRT). The abstract does not state the stereotactic dose or the stratification factors.

NCT04214262.schema_source: PubMed abstract of SWOG/NRG S1914 states the atezolizumab schedule and both arms (PMID 42702214).

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Planned external-beam technique (IMRT or VMAT versus non-IMRT or non-VMAT), FIGO 2014 stage (IB2-IIB node positive versus III-IVA), and planned total external-beam plus brachytherapy dose. The abstract cuts off before the dose cut-points.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients with newly diagnosed high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer were randomly assigned to pembrolizumab or placebo, each with chemoradiotherapy (KEYNOTE-A18).

arms.label: Pembrolizumab plus chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: Pembrolizumab with chemoradiotherapy.

arms.label: Placebo plus chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: Placebo with chemoradiotherapy.

schema.note: 1060 patients were assigned (529 pembrolizumab, 531 placebo). This abstract does not restate the pembrolizumab dose.

NCT04221945.schema_source: PubMed abstract of KEYNOTE-A18 states the stratification factors and the pembrolizumab versus placebo assignment (PMID 39288779).

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma after completion of induction chemotherapy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to reduced-volume radiotherapy based on the post-induction tumor or conventional-volume radiotherapy based on the pre-induction tumor.

arms.label: Post-induction volume
arms.text: Reduced-volume radiotherapy contoured on the post-induction chemotherapy tumor volume.

arms.label: Pre-induction volume
arms.text: Conventional-volume radiotherapy contoured on the pre-induction chemotherapy tumor volume.

schema.note: 445 patients were assigned (225 post-induction, 220 pre-induction). Prescription dose is not stated beyond the volume comparison.

NCT04384627.schema_source: PubMed abstract of the noninferiority nasopharyngeal trial states the 1:1 volume randomization (PMID 39970442).

schema.label: Design
schema.text: ENGOT-en11/GOG-3053/KEYNOTE-B21 randomized, double-blind phase III trial of adjuvant therapy for endometrial cancer. Radiotherapy was allowed with the chemotherapy platform and is not described as a separate randomized arm.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomised to pembrolizumab or placebo added to adjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel.

arms.label: Pembrolizumab
arms.text: Pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for six cycles with carboplatin and paclitaxel, then pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for six cycles.

arms.label: Placebo
arms.text: Matching placebo with the same carboplatin and paclitaxel schedule, then placebo every 6 weeks for six cycles.

schema.note: 1095 patients were randomised (545 pembrolizumab, 550 placebo).

NCT04634877.schema_source: PubMed abstract of KEYNOTE-B21 states the pembrolizumab and placebo doses and the adjuvant chemotherapy backbone (PMID 39284383).

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Locally advanced rectal cancer, cT3 N+ M0 or cT4 any N M0 (NEOTERIC).

schema.label: Design
schema.text: All patients received long-course neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, 45-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fractions with concurrent capecitabine, before the randomized immunotherapy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were then assigned 1:1 to atezolizumab plus tiragolumab or atezolizumab alone.

arms.label: Atezolizumab plus tiragolumab
arms.text: Three 21-day cycles of atezolizumab 1200 mg on day 1 plus tiragolumab 600 mg.

arms.label: Atezolizumab
arms.text: Three 21-day cycles of atezolizumab 1200 mg on day 1.

schema.note: 55 patients were assigned (28 combination, 27 atezolizumab).

NCT05009069.schema_source: PubMed abstract of NEOTERIC states the chemoradiotherapy backbone and both immunotherapy arms (PMID 41529226).

schema.label: Design
schema.text: ISRT-NPC is a multicenter open-label noninferiority phase III trial in stage I-III nasopharyngeal carcinoma with limited nodal burden. 414 patients are planned.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Institution scale and N stage.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomly assigned 1:1 to involved-site nodal irradiation or elective regional irradiation.

arms.label: Involved-site irradiation
arms.text: High-risk CTV1 receives 60 Gy and includes a 1 cm expansion of positive nodes plus level VIIa and the retrostyloid space above C1. Low-risk CTV2 receives 50 Gy and covers a 3 cm caudal expansion below C1 for N0 disease, or 3 cm below positive nodes.

arms.label: Elective regional irradiation
arms.text: Elective regional nodal irradiation, the control strategy. The protocol abstract does not restate the elective nodal dose volume beyond identifying it as the standard comparator.

NCT05145660.schema_source: PubMed abstract of the ISRT-NPC protocol states the 1:1 randomization, strata, and involved-site dose volumes (PMID 37537541).

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Locally advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (NeoRacing).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomized to perioperative chemotherapy and PD-1 antibody, with or without preoperative chemoradiation.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Perioperative chemotherapy, PD-1 antibody, and surgery, with preoperative chemoradiation, then PD-1 antibody maintenance until one year after surgery.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Perioperative chemotherapy, PD-1 antibody, and surgery, without preoperative chemoradiation, then PD-1 antibody maintenance until one year after surgery.

schema.note: The protocol abstract does not name the PD-1 antibody or restate chemotherapy and radiotherapy doses.

NCT05161572.schema_source: PubMed abstract of the NeoRacing protocol states the with-or-without preoperative chemoradiation randomization (PMID 35764956).

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Resected, high-risk, cisplatin-ineligible locally advanced squamous-cell carcinoma of the head and neck (XRay Vision). About 700 patients are planned.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1 to xevinapant or placebo, each with radiotherapy during the early cycles.

arms.label: Xevinapant
arms.text: Six cycles of xevinapant, combined with radiotherapy for the first three cycles.

arms.label: Placebo
arms.text: Six cycles of placebo, combined with radiotherapy for the first three cycles.

schema.note: This design paper does not state the xevinapant or radiotherapy dose.

NCT05386550.schema_source: PubMed abstract of the XRay Vision design paper states the 1:1 xevinapant randomization (PMID 38197296).

schema.label: Design
schema.text: PCS-XI multicenter phase III randomized trial of pelvic radiotherapy with a prostate brachytherapy boost.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomized 1:1 to conventionally fractionated or ultra-hypofractionated whole-pelvis radiotherapy. Both arms received the same brachytherapy boost and androgen deprivation.

arms.label: Conventional fractionation
arms.text: Whole-pelvis radiotherapy, 43 Gy in 20 fractions, 44 Gy in 22 fractions, or 46 Gy in 23 fractions, plus a single 15 Gy HDR brachytherapy fraction to the prostate and concomitant androgen deprivation.

arms.label: Ultra-hypofractionation
arms.text: Whole-pelvis radiotherapy, 25 Gy in 5 fractions every other day, plus a single 15 Gy HDR brachytherapy fraction to the prostate and concomitant androgen deprivation.

schema.note: 142 patients were included in the interim analysis (73 conventional, 69 ultra-hypofractionated).

NCT05820633.schema_source: PubMed abstract of the PCS-XI interim analysis states both pelvic schedules and the common HDR boost (PMID 42134662).

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Age 65 years or older, histologically confirmed newly diagnosed glioblastoma, ECOG 0-2. The protocol report identifies the trial as NCIC CTG/CCTG CE.6 with EORTC and TROG participation.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Centre, age (65-70, 71-75, or 76 or older), ECOG 0-1 versus 2, and biopsy versus resection.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomized 1:1 to short-course radiotherapy alone or the same radiotherapy with temozolomide.

arms.label: Radiotherapy
arms.text: 40 Gy in 15 fractions.

arms.label: Radiotherapy plus temozolomide
arms.text: 40 Gy in 15 fractions with 3 weeks of concomitant temozolomide, then monthly adjuvant temozolomide until progression or 12 cycles.

schema.note: Accrual was 562 patients. The abstract does not state the temozolomide milligram dose.

protocol:TROG 08.02.schema_source: Open conference abstract of the CCTG CE.6 phase III protocol states the 1:1 randomization, 40 Gy schedule, and stratification (PMC4144629).

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: High-risk localised prostate cancer, planned for radical radiotherapy with at least 12 months of androgen deprivation, and suitable for stereotactic body radiotherapy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomised to prostate stereotactic radiotherapy or to prostate plus pelvic nodal stereotactic radiotherapy.

arms.label: Prostate SBRT
arms.text: Prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy in 5 fractions on alternate days over 2 weeks. The abstract does not state the gray dose.

arms.label: Prostate and pelvic nodal SBRT
arms.text: Prostate and pelvic nodal stereotactic body radiotherapy in 5 fractions on alternate days over 2 weeks. The abstract does not state the gray dose.

schema.note: The same abstract registers the trial on ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT05613023.

protocol:Pace-Nodes.schema_source: PubMed abstract of the PACE-NODES protocol states the two five-fraction stereotactic arms and the androgen deprivation requirement (PMID 41732215).

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Age 18 years or older with invasive breast carcinoma after breast conservation or mastectomy and axillary surgery, or axillary surgery alone for an occult primary. Adjuvant radiotherapy to the breast or chest wall, with or without the axilla and internal mammary nodes, is recommended, and the estimated lifetime risk of radiation-induced late major cardiac events is at least 2%.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Participants are randomised 1:1 by the Institute of Cancer Research Clinical Trials and Statistics Unit.

arms.label: Proton beam therapy
arms.text: Proton beam therapy over 3 weeks, delivered in Manchester or London.

arms.label: Photon radiotherapy
arms.text: Tailored photon radiotherapy over 3 weeks at the local radiotherapy centre. The registry describes the photon technique as intensity-modulated arc therapy.

schema.note: The registry record does not state a gray dose.

ISRCTN14220944.schema_source: The public ISRCTN record for PARABLE states the 1:1 proton versus tailored photon randomization and the cardiac-risk entry rule.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: PARADIGM-2 is two parallel multicenter open-label non-randomized phase I dose-escalation studies. MGMT promoter methylation selects the cohort. Olaparib dose is defined by dose cohort rather than a single fixed dose.

arms.label: Parallel 1, methylated MGMT
arms.text: Partial-brain IMRT 60 Gy in 30 fractions over 6 weeks, oral temozolomide 75 mg/m2 daily throughout radiotherapy, intermittent once-daily olaparib from day 1 of radiotherapy through 4 weeks after radiotherapy, then 6 cycles of adjuvant temozolomide.

arms.label: Parallel 2, unmethylated MGMT
arms.text: Partial-brain IMRT 60 Gy in 30 fractions over 6 weeks, with continuous daily olaparib starting 3 days before radiotherapy and continuing for 4 weeks after radiotherapy, without temozolomide.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, age under 70 years, WHO performance status 0 or 1, with tumor material for an MGMT promoter methylation assay.

ISRCTN51253312.schema_source: The public ISRCTN record for PARADIGM-2 states MGMT-directed assignment and both radiotherapy and temozolomide schedules.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients with non-metastatic high-risk prostate cancer were eligible. All received 2.5 years of hormonal therapy, pelvic nodal radiotherapy, a prostate boost, and weekly docetaxel.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: The sequence of the prostate boost and whole-pelvic irradiation was randomized. Docetaxel was 20 mg/m2 on the first radiotherapy day and weekly for eight doses.

arms.label: Standard sequence
arms.text: 46.5 Gy in 25 fractions to the pelvic nodes, then a prostate boost of 26.78 Gy in 13 fractions (20.6 Gy in 10 fractions after prior prostatectomy; seminal vesicles included for T3b).

arms.label: Inverted sequence
arms.text: The same pelvic dose and prostate boost, with the boost given before whole-pelvic irradiation.

schema.note: 90 patients were randomized (42 standard sequence, 44 experimental sequence in the analyzed set). Boost doses are from the open full text.

NCT00452556.schema_source: The open ELDORADO abstract (PMID 33102224) states the randomized sequence, and the PMC full text states the prostate boost doses.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Adults with pT1 or pT2 oropharyngeal or floor-of-mouth squamous-cell carcinoma and a single ipsilateral cervical node metastasis (pN1) after curative-intent surgery were the target population.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Postoperative irradiation was compared with no adjuvant irradiation. Patients who declined randomization could be followed in an observational cohort.

arms.label: Irradiation
arms.text: Postoperative irradiation. The dose and volumes are not specified in the open protocol abstract.

arms.label: No irradiation
arms.text: No adjuvant radiotherapy after surgery.

schema.note: The protocol aimed to enroll 560 patients in a 1:1 randomization.

NCT00964977.schema_source: The open DOESAK protocol abstract (PMID 20028566) states randomization to postoperative irradiation or no irradiation.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients with nonoperable locally advanced hepatocellular carcinoma, at least one lesion larger than 7 cm, and more than 30% hepatic reserve were randomized to yttrium-90 glass microsphere dosimetry strategies.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Personalized lesion dosimetry was compared with standard treated-volume dosimetry.

arms.label: Personalized dosimetry
arms.text: At least 205 Gy to the index lesion, with a goal above 250 to 300 Gy when possible.

arms.label: Standard dosimetry
arms.text: 120 Gy plus or minus 20 Gy to the treated volume.

schema.note: 60 patients were randomized (31 personalized, 29 standard).

NCT02582034.schema_source: The updated DOSISPHERE-01 abstract (PMID 38212068) states the personalized versus standard yttrium-90 dose targets.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients with squamous-cell carcinoma of the larynx, pharynx, or oral cavity who were eligible for curative radiotherapy were enrolled.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Patients were stratified by tumor localisation, T classification, histopathological grade, and institution.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Accelerated radiotherapy was compared with conventional fractionation at the same total dose.

arms.label: Six fractions per week
arms.text: 66 to 70 Gy in 33 to 35 fractions, given as six fractions per week.

arms.label: Five fractions per week
arms.text: 66 to 70 Gy in 33 to 35 fractions, given as five fractions per week.

schema.note: 908 patients were assigned (458 accelerated, 450 conventional).

NCT00120211.schema_source: The Lancet Oncology abstract of the IAEA-ACC trial (PMID 20382075) states the five versus six fractions-per-week randomization and stratification.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Treatment-naive patients with histologically confirmed stage IIIA or IIIB non-small-cell lung cancer were eligible.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Protracted palliative radiotherapy was compared with chemotherapy followed by short-course radiotherapy.

arms.label: Radiotherapy alone
arms.text: 39 Gy in 13 fractions.

arms.label: Chemotherapy then short-course radiotherapy
arms.text: Two or three cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy, then 10 Gy in one fraction or 16 Gy in two fractions one week apart.

schema.note: 65 patients were analyzed (31 radiotherapy alone, 34 chemotherapy then radiotherapy).

NCT00864331.schema_source: The IAEA palliative lung-cancer abstract (PMID 26163093) states both randomized treatment schedules and names NCT00864331.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients with unresectable locally advanced esophageal squamous-cell carcinoma received paclitaxel and cisplatin induction chemotherapy and concurrent chemoradiotherapy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: The randomized factor was the duration of tislelizumab. Both groups received two induction cycles and two concurrent cycles.

arms.label: Group A
arms.text: Tislelizumab for 16 cycles: two with induction chemotherapy, two with concurrent chemoradiotherapy, and 12 maintenance cycles.

arms.label: Group B
arms.text: Tislelizumab for four cycles: two with induction chemotherapy and two with concurrent chemoradiotherapy, without maintenance.

schema.note: 114 patients were assigned (57 per group). Radiotherapy dose and chemotherapy milligram doses are not stated in this abstract.

NCT05520619.schema_source: The EC-CRT-002 abstract (PMID 41962116) states the two tislelizumab durations added to induction chemotherapy and chemoradiotherapy.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Participants with EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer and up to ten brain metastases amenable to stereotactic radiosurgery were eligible. This joint report covers LUOSICNS and OUTRUN.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Upfront radiosurgery plus osimertinib was compared with osimertinib alone.

arms.label: Radiosurgery plus osimertinib
arms.text: Stereotactic radiosurgery, single or multifraction, followed by osimertinib 80 mg daily.

arms.label: Osimertinib
arms.text: Osimertinib 80 mg daily without upfront radiosurgery.

schema.note: 79 participants were randomized (39 radiosurgery plus osimertinib, 40 osimertinib). The radiosurgery dose is not stated.

NCT03769103.schema_source: The STARLET joint abstract of OUTRUN and LUOSICNS (PMID 41534788) states radiosurgery plus osimertinib versus osimertinib alone.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients aged 70 years or older, judged frail by geriatric evaluation, with stage II-IV head and neck squamous-cell carcinoma treated with curative intent, were eligible.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Minimisation assigned standard fractionation or a hypofractionated split course. Physicians and patients were not masked.

arms.label: Standard fractionation
arms.text: 70 Gy in 35 fractions over 7 weeks.

arms.label: Hypofractionated split course
arms.text: 55 Gy in 20 fractions, given as two courses of 2 weeks separated by a 2-week break.

schema.note: 202 patients were assigned (102 hypofractionated split course, 100 standard fractionation).

NCT01864850.schema_source: The ELAN-RT abstract (PMID 41713468) states both radiotherapy schedules in frail older patients.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Women aged 18 years or older with WHO performance score 0 to 2 and high-risk endometrial cancer (FIGO 2009 stage I grade 3 with deep myometrial invasion and/or lymphovascular invasion, stage II-III, or stage I-III serous or clear-cell histology) were eligible.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Biased-coin minimisation was stratified by participating centre, lymphadenectomy, stage, and histological type.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Pelvic radiotherapy alone was compared with the same radiotherapy plus chemotherapy.

arms.label: Pelvic radiotherapy
arms.text: 48.6 Gy in fractions of 1.8 Gy.

arms.label: Chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: The same pelvic radiotherapy with cisplatin 50 mg/m2 intravenously in weeks 1 and 4, followed by four cycles of carboplatin AUC 5 and paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 every 3 weeks.

schema.note: 660 eligible patients were assigned (330 per group).

NCT00411138.schema_source: The Lancet Oncology 10-year PORTEC-3 abstract (PMID 40921169) states eligibility, stratification, and both adjuvant arms.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients with stage II-III thoracic esophageal squamous-cell carcinoma were randomized 1:1.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Elective nodal irradiation was compared with involved-field irradiation. Both used the same stated dose ranges.

arms.label: Elective nodal irradiation
arms.text: 1.8 to 2.0 Gy per day to 60.0 to 66.0 Gy to the gross tumor volume and 50.0 to 54.0 Gy to the clinical target volume, with elective nodal coverage.

arms.label: Involved-field irradiation
arms.text: The same dose ranges limited to an involved field.

schema.note: 228 patients from nine centres were randomly assigned. Concurrent chemotherapy is not described in this long-term abstract.

NCT01551589.schema_source: The esophageal ENI versus involved-field abstract (PMID 32841543) states the randomized fields and dose ranges.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients were randomized after surgery for atypical meningioma.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Adjuvant fractionated radiotherapy was compared with observation.

arms.label: Radiotherapy
arms.text: 60 Gy in 30 fractions.

arms.label: Observation
arms.text: Observation after surgery.

protocol:TROG 15.02.schema_source: The open ROAM/EORTC-1308 radiotherapy quality-assurance abstract states randomization to 60 Gy in 30 fractions or observation.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients with axillary node-positive breast cancer who received postoperative irradiation were randomized.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Prolonged low-dose chemotherapy was compared with no chemotherapy.

arms.label: CMF
arms.text: Monthly CMF for 2 years: cyclophosphamide 50 mg/m2 orally on days 1 to 14, methotrexate 15 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1 and 8, and fluorouracil 350 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1 and 8.

arms.label: Control
arms.text: Surgery and postoperative irradiation without adjuvant chemotherapy.

schema.note: 452 patients were randomized.

protocol:EORTC-09771.schema_source: The 10-year EORTC 09771 abstract (PMID 7799039) states prolonged low-dose CMF versus no chemotherapy after postoperative irradiation.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Women with completely excised ductal carcinoma in situ smaller than 5 cm were eligible.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Local excision alone was compared with local excision plus radiotherapy.

arms.label: Local excision
arms.text: No further treatment after complete local excision.

arms.label: Local excision plus radiotherapy
arms.text: Radiotherapy after complete local excision. The dose is not stated in this abstract.

schema.note: 1010 women were assigned (503 excision alone, 507 excision plus radiotherapy).

protocol:EORTC-10853.schema_source: The 15-year EORTC 10853 abstract (PMID 24043739) states randomization to local excision alone or local excision plus radiotherapy.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients with limited-stage small-cell lung cancer in complete remission after chemotherapy and thoracic radiotherapy were eligible.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomisation was stratified by medical centre, age, and the interval from the start of induction treatment to randomisation.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Standard-dose prophylactic cranial irradiation was compared with a higher total dose.

arms.label: Standard dose
arms.text: 25 Gy in 10 daily fractions of 2.5 Gy.

arms.label: Higher dose
arms.text: 36 Gy, given either as 18 daily fractions of 2 Gy or as 24 fractions of 1.5 Gy in 16 days with two daily sessions at least 6 hours apart.

schema.note: 720 patients were assigned, 360 to each total-dose group.

NCT00005062.schema_source: The Lancet Oncology abstract of PCI 99-01/EORTC 22003-08004 (PMID 19386548) states both cranial-irradiation dose arms and the stratification factors.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Adults with WHO grade II astrocytoma, oligoastrocytoma, or oligodendroglioma, WHO performance status 0 to 2, no prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy, and at least one high-risk feature (age over 40 years, progression, size over 5 cm, midline crossing, or neurological symptoms) were eligible.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Minimisation used institution, 1p deletion (absent, present, or undetermined), contrast enhancement, age under 40 versus 40 years or older, and WHO performance status 0 versus 1 or higher.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Primary radiotherapy was compared with primary temozolomide.

arms.label: Radiotherapy
arms.text: Conformal radiotherapy up to 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions of 1.8 Gy, once daily, 5 days per week.

arms.label: Temozolomide
arms.text: Temozolomide 75 mg/m2 once daily for 21 days, repeated every 28 days, for a maximum of 12 cycles.

schema.note: 477 patients were randomly assigned (240 radiotherapy, 237 temozolomide).

NCT00182819.schema_source: The Lancet Oncology abstract of EORTC 22033-26033 (PMID 27686946), which names NCT00182819, states eligibility, stratification, and both arms.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: After surgery, adults with low-grade astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma, mixed oligoastrocytoma, or incompletely resected pilocytic astrocytoma and WHO performance status 0 to 2 were eligible.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Early radiotherapy was compared with radiotherapy deferred until progression.

arms.label: Early radiotherapy
arms.text: 54 Gy in fractions of 1.8 Gy after surgery.

arms.label: Deferred radiotherapy
arms.text: Radiotherapy withheld until progression.

schema.note: 314 patients were assigned (157 early radiotherapy, 157 control).

protocol:EORTC-22845.schema_source: The Lancet abstract of EORTC 22845 (PMID 16168780) states early 54 Gy radiotherapy versus radiotherapy deferred until progression.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients with T2, T3, or T4 head and neck cancer, excluding hypopharynx, were treated with curative radiotherapy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Accelerated hyperfractionation was compared with conventional fractionation.

arms.label: Accelerated fractionation
arms.text: 72 Gy in 45 fractions over 5 weeks.

arms.label: Conventional fractionation
arms.text: 70 Gy in 35 fractions over 7 weeks.

schema.note: 512 patients were accrued.

protocol:EORTC-22851.schema_source: The EORTC 22851 abstract (PMID 9288839) states 72 Gy in 45 fractions over 5 weeks versus 70 Gy in 35 fractions over 7 weeks.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients younger than 80 years with WHO performance status 0 to 2 and newly diagnosed T1-2 WHO grade 3, or T3-4 any grade, prostatic adenocarcinoma were eligible.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Minimisation used institution, clinical stage, pelvic lymph-node dissection result, and extent of the irradiation fields.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: External irradiation alone was compared with the same irradiation plus long-term androgen suppression.

arms.label: Radiotherapy
arms.text: 50 Gy to the whole pelvis plus 20 Gy to the prostate and seminal vesicles, one fraction per day, 5 days a week, for 7 weeks.

arms.label: Radiotherapy plus androgen suppression
arms.text: The same radiotherapy plus goserelin acetate 3.6 mg subcutaneously every 4 weeks for 3 years, with cyproterone acetate 50 mg orally three times a day for 1 month starting 1 week before the first goserelin dose.

schema.note: 415 patients were assigned (208 radiotherapy, 207 combined treatment).

NCT00849082.schema_source: The Lancet Oncology abstract of EORTC 22863 (PMID 20933466) states eligibility, minimisation factors, and both arms.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients with stage I or II breast cancer and a microscopically complete excision were treated with breast-conserving surgery.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Minimisation used age, menopausal status, extensive ductal carcinoma in situ, clinical tumor size, nodal status, and institution.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: After whole-breast irradiation, a tumor-bed boost was compared with no boost.

arms.label: No boost
arms.text: Whole-breast irradiation of 50 Gy in 5 weeks and no boost.

arms.label: Boost
arms.text: The same 50 Gy whole-breast irradiation plus a 16 Gy boost.

schema.note: 5318 patients were assigned (2657 no boost, 2661 boost).

NCT02295033.schema_source: The 20-year EORTC boost abstract (PMID 25500422) states the 50 Gy whole-breast randomization with or without a 16 Gy boost and the minimisation factors.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Men aged 75 years or younger with untreated cT0-3 prostate cancer and WHO performance status 0 or 1 were enrolled after radical prostatectomy for cancer extending beyond the prostate.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Immediate postoperative irradiation was compared with a wait-and-see policy.

arms.label: Postoperative irradiation
arms.text: 60 Gy of conventional irradiation to the surgical bed over 6 weeks.

arms.label: Wait and see

arms.text: 3.7 GBq iodine-131 after recombinant human thyroid-stimulating hormone.

arms.label: High dose, withdrawal
arms.text: 3.7 GBq iodine-131 after thyroid hormone withdrawal.

schema.note: 438 patients were randomly assigned.

NCT00415233.schema_source: The HiLo long-term abstract (PMID 30501974) states the four-way randomization of iodine dose and preparation.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Intermediate-risk localized prostate cancer by the D'Amico grouping (not low risk and not high risk: clinical stage, PSA, and biopsy Gleason score).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: All patients receive 3 months of neoadjuvant androgen deprivation, then iodine-125 transperineal brachytherapy planned to at least 144 Gy to the clinical target volume (prostate plus margin). They are then randomized to adjuvant androgen deprivation or no further androgen deprivation.

arms.label: Adjuvant ADT
arms.text: Nine months of adjuvant androgen deprivation after iodine-125 brachytherapy.

arms.label: No adjuvant ADT
arms.text: Iodine-125 brachytherapy without adjuvant androgen deprivation.

schema.note: Stratification factors are not stated in the protocol paper.

NCT00664456.schema_source: The open-access SHIP 0804 protocol (PMID 20964826) states the randomization after neoadjuvant androgen deprivation and the iodine-125 dose.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Non-small cell lung cancer with a postoperative radiotherapy indication (more than pN1 and/or R1). Photons or protons are allowed in both arms.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified by staging with or without PET-CT, resection status R1 or R0, and study center.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients with R0 or R1 resection are randomized 1:1. The mediastinal target is treated to 50 Gy in 2 Gy fractions. A 10 Gy boost (total 60 Gy) is added for R1 resection or extracapsular extension. The randomized comparison is fractions per week, not total dose.

arms.label: Accelerated
arms.text: Seven fractions per week, 2 Gy per fraction (50 Gy, or 60 Gy with the R1 or extracapsular boost).

arms.label: Conventional
arms.text: Five fractions per week, 2 Gy per fraction, using the same total-dose rules.

schema.note: Patients with R2 resection or postoperative recurrence are a separate stratum and receive 66 Gy in 2 Gy fractions at five fractions per week, not the accelerated schedule.

NCT02189967.schema_source: The open-access PORTAF protocol (PMID 29262836) states accelerated versus conventional postoperative radiotherapy and the risk-based doses.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Chronic active neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Multicentre double-masked trial. Participants are randomized 2:1 in favour of radiation. Everyone receives a baseline intravitreal injection of 0.5 mg ranibizumab, then monthly visits for 24 months with ranibizumab if retreatment criteria are met.

arms.label: Stereotactic radiotherapy
arms.text: A single 16 Gy stereotactic radiotherapy treatment plus as-needed ranibizumab.

arms.label: Sham
arms.text: Sham radiotherapy plus the same as-needed ranibizumab schedule.

NCT02243878.schema_source: The open-access STAR trial protocol (PMID 27881184) states 16 Gy stereotactic radiotherapy versus sham, both with ranibizumab.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Newly diagnosed T2-4 N0-2 M0 squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx treated with definitive radiotherapy. Recurrent disease, prior head and neck oncologic surgery, and concomitant chemotherapy or EGFR inhibitors are excluded.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Allocation is 2:1 to the intervention, balanced by minimization for institution, tumor site, T stage, N stage, and HPV status.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both arms use IMRT or VMAT with simultaneous integrated boost, 33 fractions in 5 weeks. High-risk gross disease is 66 Gy (2.00 Gy) and high-risk CTV is 62 Gy (1.88 Gy) in both arms.

arms.label: De-escalated elective dose
arms.text: Adds an intermediate-risk level of 58 Gy (1.76 Gy) and lowers the elective low-risk neck to 42 Gy (1.27 Gy).

arms.label: Standard elective dose
arms.text: No intermediate level. Elective low-risk neck is 48 Gy (1.45 Gy).

NCT02442375.schema_source: The open-access UPGRADE-RT protocol (PMID 28327089) states the elective-dose randomization and the dose levels.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Biopsy-proven rectal adenocarcinoma staged by CT and MRI as cT3b or less (up to 5 mm of extramural spread), N0 M0.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Three-arm feasibility randomization. In both organ-saving arms, a complete clinical response goes to active surveillance and an incomplete response goes to local excision (transanal endoscopic microsurgery or another transanal technique).

arms.label: TME
arms.text: Standard total mesorectal excision.

arms.label: Long-course chemoradiation
arms.text: Capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily on radiotherapy days and 50 Gy in 25 fractions of 2 Gy to the primary tumor and surrounding mesorectum, then surveillance or local excision by response.

arms.label: Short-course radiotherapy
arms.text: 25 Gy in five fractions of 5 Gy to the primary tumor and surrounding mesorectum, then surveillance or local excision by response.

NCT02945566.schema_source: The open-access STAR-TREC feasibility protocol (PMID 29288190) states the three-arm randomization and the radiotherapy schedules.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients older than 70 years with stage IIA-IVB (UICC 2002; stage IVB only if spread is limited to supraclavicular or celiac nodes) squamous cell carcinoma or adenocarcinoma of the esophagus or gastroesophageal junction.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is 1:1, stratified by disease stage and study site.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both arms use definitive simultaneous integrated boost radiotherapy: 50.4 Gy to the planning target volume and 59.92 Gy to the planning gross tumor volume in 28 fractions.

arms.label: SIB alone
arms.text: Radiotherapy without S-1.

arms.label: SIB plus S-1
arms.text: The same radiotherapy concurrent with S-1 (40, 50, or 60 mg twice daily by body surface area), then four consolidation cycles of S-1 on days 1-14 of each 21-day cycle.

NCT02979691.schema_source: The open-access 3JECROG P-01 protocol (PMID 31036088) states SIB radiotherapy with or without S-1 and the stratification.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Hepatocellular carcinoma or oligometastatic disease to the liver suitable for stereotactic ablative radiotherapy. This is a single-arm phase II study of kilovoltage intrafraction monitoring, not a randomized dose comparison.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: All treated patients receive liver SABR with kilovoltage intrafraction monitoring. The radiation oncologist chooses a protocol dose according to histology and clinical scenario.

arms.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
arms.text: Five fractions of 50, 45, 40, 35, 30, or 27.5 Gy, over 5-15 days.

arms.label: Liver metastases
arms.text: Preferably three fractions (54, 51, 48, 45, or 42 Gy on alternate days) or five fractions (60, 55, 50, 45, or 40 Gy).

schema.note: Dose levels are prescription options, not randomized arms.

NCT02984566.schema_source: The open-access TROG 17.03 LARK protocol (PMID 33941111) states the single-arm liver SABR dose menus used with kilovoltage intrafraction monitoring.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Breast, prostate, or non-small cell lung cancer with up to three bone-only metastases.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is 1:1, stratified by synchronous versus metachronous metastases and by primary site (prostate, breast, or lung).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Standard systemic treatment is given in both arms. For SBRT, acceptable regimens are 35 Gy in 7 fractions or 27 Gy in 3 fractions, depending on site and normal-tissue constraints.

arms.label: Standard care plus SBRT
arms.text: Systemic standard of care plus SBRT to all bone metastases.

arms.label: Standard care
arms.text: Systemic standard of care without SBRT.

NCT03143322.schema_source: The open-access STEREO-OS protocol (PMID 33541288) states randomization to standard care with or without bone SBRT and the stratification.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Unresectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, stage IIA-IVB (UICC 2002; stage IVB only for supraclavicular or celiac nodes).

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is 1:1, stratified by disease stage and tumor site.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both arms use SIB-IMRT: 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions of 1.8 Gy to the planning target volume and 59.92 Gy in 28 fractions of 2.14 Gy to the planning gross tumor volume.

arms.label: SIB alone
arms.text: Radiotherapy without concurrent chemotherapy.

arms.label: SIB plus chemotherapy
arms.text: The same radiotherapy plus weekly paclitaxel 45-60 mg/m2 and a platinum agent (nedaplatin, lobaplatin, or cisplatin) 20-25 mg/m2 for 5-6 weeks. Consolidation chemotherapy is recommended for fit patients.

NCT03308552.schema_source: The open-access 3JECROG P-02 protocol (PMID 32962674) states SIB radiotherapy with or without weekly paclitaxel and platinum.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Severe coeliac-plexus pain (average BPI pain at least 5) and ECOG performance status 0-2. Pancreatic cancer and other cancers invading the coeliac plexus are eligible.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase II radiosurgery. There is no comparator arm.

arms.label: Coeliac plexus radiosurgery
arms.text: A single fraction with 25 Gy prescribed to coeliac-plexus voxels at least 1 cm from bowel. Dose painting lowers the prescription to 15 Gy at 0.5-1 cm from bowel, 10 Gy within 0.5 cm of bowel, and 20 Gy in the 0.5 cm expansion.

NCT03323489.schema_source: The open-access coeliac plexus radiosurgery protocol (PMID 35332036) states the single-arm 25 Gy prescription.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Intraprostatic recurrence only at least 2 years after external radiotherapy, Phoenix definition, stage T1-T2, PSA 10 ng/mL or less, PSA doubling time longer than 10 months, and no pelvic or metastatic disease on choline or PSMA PET.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Phase I selects one salvage SBRT schedule with a time-to-event continual reassessment method, using grade 3 or higher gastrointestinal or urinary toxicity, or any grade 4 event, within 18 weeks. Phase II then tests that selected schedule as a single arm. Five or six fractions are given over a maximum of 12 days.

arms.label: 5 x 6 Gy
arms.text: Candidate schedule, 30 Gy in five fractions.

arms.label: 6 x 6 Gy
arms.text: Candidate schedule, 36 Gy in six fractions.

arms.label: 5 x 5 Gy
arms.text: Candidate schedule, 25 Gy in five fractions.

schema.note: The three schedules are dose-finding options. Patients are not randomized among them in parallel.

NCT03438552.schema_source: The open-access GETUG-AFU 31 protocol (PMID 31377694) states the salvage prostate SBRT dose levels selected by continual reassessment.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Clinically node-positive breast cancer. Tailored axillary surgery removes the sentinel nodes, palpable disease, and the clipped biopsy-positive node.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Randomization is 1:1 by minimization. Everyone receives whole-breast radiotherapy after breast conservation or chest-wall radiotherapy after mastectomy, plus regional nodal radiotherapy. Breast or chest wall and regional nodes: 50 Gy in 25 fractions, 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions, or a hypofractionated 40 Gy in 15 fractions.

arms.label: TAS plus dissection
arms.text: Tailored axillary surgery, then axillary dissection, with nodal radiotherapy excluding the dissected axilla (levels II/III, medial supraclavicular, and internal mammary nodes).

arms.label: TAS plus full axillary radiotherapy
arms.text: Tailored axillary surgery without axillary dissection, with nodal radiotherapy including the full axilla (levels I-III, medial supraclavicular, and internal mammary nodes).

schema.note: The protocol names minimization factors but the factor list is not printed in the open text.

NCT03513614.schema_source: The open-access TAXIS protocol (PMID 30514362) states tailored axillary surgery with or without axillary dissection and the nodal radiotherapy volumes.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: PET-detected pelvic nodal oligorecurrence (up to five nodes) after radical local treatment for prostate cancer (prostatectomy, radiotherapy, or both).

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is 1:1, stratified by PET tracer (choline, fluciclovine, or PSMA) and by metastasis-directed therapy (salvage lymph node dissection or SBRT).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both arms receive 6 months of androgen deprivation plus metastasis-directed therapy. SBRT, when used, is 30 Gy in 3 fractions, prescribed so that the 80% isodose (30 Gy) covers 90% of the PTV, with fractions separated by more than 48 and less than 96 hours.

arms.label: MDT plus ADT
arms.text: Salvage nodal dissection or SBRT, plus 6 months of ADT, without elective pelvic radiotherapy.

arms.label: WPRT plus MDT plus ADT
arms.text: Elective pelvic nodes 45 Gy in 25 fractions of 1.8 Gy, with an integrated boost to the nodal GTV of median 65 Gy in 25 fractions (2.6 Gy), plus metastasis-directed therapy and 6 months of ADT. Prostate-bed radiotherapy, if given, is at least 66 Gy in 33 fractions.

NCT03569241.schema_source: The open-access PEACE V STORM protocol (PMID 32398040) states metastasis-directed therapy with or without whole pelvic radiotherapy, both with 6 months of ADT.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients with bone metastases for whom the radiation oncologist prescribes either 8 Gy in 1 fraction or 20 Gy in 5 fractions. The trial is aimed at metastases in the lower spine and pelvis.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is 1:1, stratified by prescribed dose: 8 Gy in 1 fraction versus 20 Gy in 5 fractions.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: The prescribed dose is the same in both arms. If several bone metastases are treated in one course, they all use the assigned technique.

arms.label: Simple unplanned radiotherapy
arms.text: Simple unplanned palliative radiotherapy to 8 Gy in 1 fraction or 20 Gy in 5 fractions.

arms.label: VMAT
arms.text: 3D conformal volumetric modulated arc therapy to the same prescribed dose.

NCT03694015.schema_source: The open-access SUPR-3D protocol (PMID 31660894) states randomization between simple unplanned palliative radiotherapy and VMAT at 8 Gy or 20 Gy.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Siewert type II or III esophagogastric junction adenocarcinoma after transabdominal radical surgery and D2 lymphadenectomy, pathological stage IIB to IIIC.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is 1:1, stratified by whether the esophagogastric junction is invaded and by postoperative stage.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: SOX is oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 plus S-1 orally twice daily for 14 days. S-1 is 40, 50, or 60 mg per dose for body surface area below 1.25, 1.25 to below 1.5, and 1.5 or higher.

arms.label: SOX alone
arms.text: Eight cycles of adjuvant SOX.

arms.label: SOX plus chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: Two cycles of SOX, then 45 Gy in 25 fractions of 1.8 Gy with S-1 twice daily on Monday through Friday during radiotherapy, then four further cycles of SOX.

NCT03973008.schema_source: The open-access ARTEG protocol (PMID 34717717) states adjuvant SOX chemotherapy with or without 45 Gy chemoradiotherapy after D2 resection.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Treatment-naive, biopsy-supported borderline resectable or locally advanced pancreatic cancer.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase II. After the planned chemoradiotherapy, the investigator chooses continued chemotherapy or surgery.

arms.label: Split-course SBRT plus chemotherapy
arms.text: Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 then gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle for six cycles. During the first two cycles, SBRT is one 10 Gy fraction on days 2 and 16 (four fractions of 10 Gy).

NCT04289792.schema_source: The open-access splitPC protocol (PMID 33154057) states the single-arm nab-paclitaxel, gemcitabine, and split-course SBRT schedule.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Previously untreated unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer in patients unfit for chemotherapy. No elective nodal irradiation is used.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Durvalumab 1500 mg intravenously on day 1 and every 4 weeks for up to 12 months (maximum 13 doses) starts in both groups, and radiotherapy starts within 72 hours of the first dose. A hypofractionated safety lead-in uses sequential allocation; expansion then assigns arms with a biased-coin randomization.

arms.label: Conventional fractionation
arms.text: Durvalumab plus 30 fractions of 2 Gy (60 Gy) over about 6 weeks.

arms.label: Hypofractionated
arms.text: Durvalumab plus 20 fractions of 2.75 Gy (55 Gy) over about 4 weeks.

NCT04351256.schema_source: The open-access TRADE-hypo protocol (PMID 32842974) states durvalumab with either 60 Gy conventional or 55 Gy hypofractionated thoracic radiotherapy.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Microsatellite-stable locally advanced colon adenocarcinoma that is clinically T4 or has bulky nodes.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is 1:1, stratified by tumor location and N stage.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: CAPOX is oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 and capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 orally on days 1-14, every 3 weeks. Both arms have curative surgery and then four further cycles of CAPOX.

arms.label: CAPOX
arms.text: Four cycles of preoperative CAPOX, then surgery, then four cycles of CAPOX.

arms.label: SCRT plus CAPOX plus serplulimab
arms.text: Short-course radiotherapy 25 Gy in 5 fractions, then four cycles of CAPOX plus serplulimab 300 mg intravenously on day 1 every 3 weeks, then surgery, then four cycles of CAPOX.

NCT05732493.schema_source: The open-access TORCH-C protocol (PMID 38309748) states CAPOX with or without short-course radiotherapy and serplulimab.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Biopsy-proven unfavourable intermediate-risk or favourable high-risk prostate cancer (ISUP 3-5 and/or cT2b-T3a N0 and/or PSA 10-20, without T3b/T4 or PSA above 20). ECOG 0-1. High-risk patients need PSMA PET showing N0 M0. Prostate volume under 100 cc.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Every patient receives 6 months of androgen deprivation. Randomization is between two stereotactic schedules.

arms.label: SBRT monotherapy
arms.text: 40 Gy in five fractions on alternating days.

arms.label: Virtual HDR boost
arms.text: 20 Gy in two fractions given 1 week apart, then 2 weeks later 36 Gy in 12 fractions, five fractions per week.

schema.note: Stratification factors are not stated in the protocol abstract or the extracted methods text.

protocol:TROG 18.01.schema_source: The open-access TROG 18.01 NINJA protocol (PMID 31434782) states randomization between two prostate SBRT schedules, both with 6 months of androgen deprivation.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: In the SCOPE2 PET substudy, patients received induction cisplatin 60 mg/m2 plus capecitabine 625 mg/m2 on days 1-21. All patients, including PET responders, were randomized to standard-dose or high-dose radiotherapy given over 25 fractions.

arms.label: 50 Gy
arms.text: Standard-dose definitive chemoradiotherapy, 50 Gy.

arms.label: 60 Gy
arms.text: High-dose definitive chemoradiotherapy, 60 Gy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients whose day-14 PET showed less than a 35% fall in SUVmax were randomized to stay on cisplatin/capecitabine or switch chemotherapy for one further induction cycle and then concurrently with radiotherapy. Responders stayed on cisplatin/capecitabine.

arms.label: Continue cisplatin/capecitabine
arms.text: Cisplatin 60 mg/m2 and capecitabine 625 mg/m2 on days 1-21.

arms.label: Switch to carboplatin/paclitaxel
arms.text: Carboplatin AUC 5 and paclitaxel 175 mg/m2.

schema.note: A separate qualitative report also describes participants assigned to carboplatin/paclitaxel or cisplatin/capecitabine with either dose. This record uses the doses printed in the PET substudy.

NCT02741856.schema_source: The open SCOPE2 PET substudy report (PMID 37409323) states the 50 Gy versus 60 Gy randomization and the chemotherapy switch for early PET non-responders.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients aged 3-25 years with residual or progressive benign or low-grade brain tumors.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Phase III randomization 1:1. Both arms received 54 Gy in 30 fractions over 6 weeks.

arms.label: Stereotactic conformal radiotherapy
arms.text: High-precision stereotactic conformal radiotherapy, 54 Gy in 30 fractions.

arms.label: Conventional radiotherapy
arms.text: Conventional radiotherapy, 54 Gy in 30 fractions.

schema.note: Stratification factors are not stated in the open trial report.

NCT00517959.schema_source: The open randomized trial report (PMID 28570730) states stereotactic conformal radiotherapy versus conventional radiotherapy, both 54 Gy in 30 fractions.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Locally advanced rectal cancer, cT3-4 or node positive, planned for neoadjuvant treatment.

schema.text: During long-course chemoradiotherapy, patients are randomized to MR-guided adaptive radiotherapy with a simultaneous integrated boost or to intensity-modulated radiotherapy. arms.label: MRgART with SIB
arms.text: 60-65 Gy in 25-28 fractions to the primary tumor and positive nodes, and 50-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fractions to the pelvis.

arms.label: IMRT
arms.text: 50-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fractions.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Breast cancer at low risk of local recurrence after conservative surgery. The trial plans to randomize 2800 patients.

arms.label: APBI

arms.label: Standard whole breast
arms.text: Standard whole-breast radiotherapy over 6.5 weeks.

arms.label: Hypofractionated whole breast
arms.text: Hypofractionated whole-breast radiotherapy over 3 weeks.

NCT01247233.schema_source: The open SHARE trial description (PMID 23598908) states the three radiotherapy schedules by technique and duration.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

schema.text: Factorial randomization 1:1:1:1. Every group received 60 Gy in 30 fractions and two cycles of concurrent paclitaxel plus cisplatin.

arms.label: ENI plus erlotinib
arms.text: Elective nodal irradiation, concurrent paclitaxel/cisplatin, plus erlotinib.

arms.label: ENI
arms.text: Elective nodal irradiation and concurrent paclitaxel/cisplatin.

arms.label: CFI plus erlotinib

arms.label: CFI

NCT00686114.schema_source: The open long-term report (PMID 32958820) states the four-arm factorial design of elective versus conventional fields, with or without erlotinib, at 60 Gy in 30 fractions.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Treatment-naive EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma with synchronous oligometastases (up to 5 metastases and no more than 2 lesions in any one organ) and no brain metastases.

schema.text: All patients received a first-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (gefitinib, erlotinib, or icotinib). Randomization was upfront radiotherapy versus no radiotherapy.

arms.label: TKI alone
arms.text: First-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor without radiotherapy.

arms.label: TKI plus radiotherapy
arms.text: The same TKI plus 25-40 Gy in 5 fractions, dose depending on tumor size and location, to all metastases and to the primary tumor and involved regional lymphatics.

schema.note: Stratification factors are not stated in the open interim report.

NCT02893332.schema_source: The open SINDAS interim report (PMID 35094066) states first-generation EGFR TKI with or without 25-40 Gy in 5 fractions to all disease sites.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Children and young adults aged 3-21 years with newly diagnosed medulloblastoma.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Patients were assigned to average-risk or high-risk treatment by metastatic status and extent of resection. This is risk-adapted therapy, not a randomization between the two craniospinal doses.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Risk-adapted craniospinal photon irradiation, a tumor-bed boost, then four cycles of high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell rescue. The chemotherapy drug names are not stated in these open abstracts.

arms.label: Average risk
arms.text: Craniospinal irradiation 23.4 Gy and a boost to 55.8 Gy to the tumor bed.

arms.label: High risk
arms.text: Craniospinal irradiation 36-39.6 Gy and a boost to 55.8 Gy to the tumor bed.

NCT00085202.schema_source: Open SJMB03 reports (PMID 33405951 and PMID 34714708) state risk-adapted craniospinal doses, a 55.8 Gy tumor-bed boost, and four cycles of high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell rescue.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Microsatellite-stable metastatic adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum, as third-line treatment.

schema.text: Patients are randomized to regorafenib alone or to regorafenib plus toripalimab with high-dose and low-dose radiotherapy.

arms.label: Regorafenib
arms.text: Regorafenib 120 mg once daily on days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle.

arms.label: Regorafenib, toripalimab, and radiotherapy
arms.text: One cycle of regorafenib 80 mg once daily on days 1-21 and toripalimab 240 mg every 3 weeks, then high-dose radiotherapy (4-8 fractions of 8-12 Gy) and low-dose radiotherapy (1-10 Gy at 0.5-2 Gy per fraction), then continued regorafenib and toripalimab.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: pN1 breast cancer after breast-conserving surgery and taxane-based adjuvant chemotherapy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Phase III noninferiority randomization of regional nodal irradiation added to whole-breast irradiation versus whole-breast irradiation alone. Fraction doses are not stated in this open report.

arms.label: Whole breast plus regional nodes
arms.text: Whole-breast irradiation plus regional node irradiation.

arms.label: Whole breast only
arms.text: Whole-breast irradiation without regional node irradiation.

NCT03269981.schema_source: The open KROG 17-01 report (PMID 39326505) states randomization to whole-breast irradiation with or without regional node irradiation.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Locally advanced rectal cancer (cT3-4, node positive, or extramural vascular invasion). Planned accrual 364, randomized 1:1. Surgery is total mesorectal excision.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Experimental treatment is short-course radiotherapy then four cycles of FOLFOX (oxaliplatin, 5-fluorouracil, and folinic acid), with surgery 2-5 weeks after the last chemotherapy cycle. Control treatment is long-course chemoradiotherapy, with surgery 6-8 weeks after radiotherapy.

arms.label: Short-course radiotherapy plus FOLFOX

arms.label: Long-course chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: 45-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fractions, five times a week, concurrent with capecitabine or 5-fluorouracil.

schema.note: FOLFOX milligram doses are not stated in the open protocol abstract.

NCT05673772.schema_source: The open SOLAR protocol (PMID 37923987) states short-course radiotherapy plus FOLFOX versus long-course chemoradiotherapy with capecitabine or 5-fluorouracil.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma after biopsy or surgery. Planned randomization of 220 patients.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Stratification is by surgical status and MGMT status.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both arms use concomitant temozolomide and 6 months of temozolomide maintenance.

arms.label: Standard dose
arms.text: 60 Gy to contrast enhancement plus a 2 cm margin (Stupp radiochemotherapy).

arms.label: MRSI-guided boost
arms.text: The same 60 Gy plan plus a simultaneous integrated boost of 72 Gy in 2.4 Gy fractions to MR spectroscopic volumes with choline/NAA greater than 2 and to contrast-enhancing lesions or the resection cavity.

NCT01507506.schema_source: The open SPECTRO-GLIO protocol (PMID 30791889) states 60 Gy radiochemotherapy versus the same treatment plus a 72 Gy MR spectroscopic boost, stratified by surgery and MGMT.

schema.label: Entry

schema.text: Both arms receive carbon-ion radiotherapy. The experimental arm adds concurrent camrelizumab.

arms.label: Carbon-ion radiotherapy
arms.text: 63 Gy (RBE) in 21 fractions.

arms.label: Carbon ions plus camrelizumab
arms.text: The same 63 Gy (RBE) in 21 fractions plus camrelizumab 200 mg intravenously every 2 weeks for up to 1 year.

NCT04143984.schema_source: The open protocol (PMID 38205914) states carbon-ion radiotherapy, 63 Gy (RBE) in 21 fractions, with or without camrelizumab.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Histologically confirmed nasopharyngeal carcinoma meeting the trial eligibility criteria. Ninety patients were enrolled.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Randomized comparison of two IMRT planning approaches. The prescription dose in Gy is not stated in the open report.

arms.label: Superficial parotid-lobe sparing IMRT

schema.label: Design
schema.text: PLATO is an integrated platform of ACT3, ACT4, and ACT5. ACT3 participants are registered, not randomized: margins greater than 1 mm are observed, and margins 1 mm or less receive lower-dose chemoradiotherapy. ACT4 and ACT5 are randomized and use concurrent chemotherapy.

schema.text: ACT3 observation is no further treatment after local excision. The ACT3 intervention is 41.4 Gy in 23 fractions to PTV_A with mitomycin C 12 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 and capecitabine 852 mg/m2 orally twice daily on radiotherapy days for 23 days.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: ACT4 minimisation factors: T stage (T1, T2), N stage (N0, NX), sex, HIV status, and centre. ACT5 factors: T stage (T2/3, T4), N stage (NX/0/1, N2/3), sex, HIV status, chemotherapy regimen (5-FU or capecitabine), and centre.

arms.label: ACT4 reduced
arms.text: IMRT with PTV_A 41.4 Gy in 23 fractions and PTV_E 34.5 Gy in 23 fractions, plus the same mitomycin and capecitabine schedule for 23 days.

arms.label: ACT5 standard
arms.text: IMRT with PTV_A 53.2 Gy in 28 fractions, involved nodes 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions if 3 cm or smaller and 53.2 Gy if larger, and PTV_E 40.0 Gy in 28 fractions.

arms.label: ACT5 boost 58.8 Gy
arms.text: IMRT with PTV_A 53.2 Gy, a synchronous boost to 58.8 Gy, involved nodes 53.2 Gy, and PTV_E 40.0 Gy, all in 28 fractions.

arms.label: ACT5 boost 61.6 Gy
arms.text: IMRT with PTV_A 53.2 Gy, a synchronous boost to 61.6 Gy, involved nodes 53.2 Gy, and PTV_E 40.0 Gy, all in 28 fractions.

schema.text: ACT4 is randomized 1:2, standard to reduced dose. ACT5 pilot and phase 2 are randomized 1:1:1 among standard dose and two increased-dose arms. The phase 3 wording also says 1:1:1, between standard-dose IMRT plus chemotherapy and an increased-dose IMRT arm with a synchronous boost plus chemotherapy.
schema.note: All ACT5 arms use centre-choice chemotherapy: mitomycin C 12 mg/m2 on day 1 with capecitabine 852 mg/m2 twice daily on radiotherapy days for 28 days, or mitomycin C 12 mg/m2 on day 1 with 5-FU 1000 mg/m2 per 24 hours on days 1-4 and 29-32.

schema.text: POTENTIAL is a prospective multicenter open-label phase 3 trial of internal mammary node irradiation after mastectomy in high-risk axillary node-positive breast cancer. Planned enrollment is 1800. Patients are required to receive at least six cycles of anthracycline and/or taxane-based chemotherapy.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified by institution, tumor location (medial or central versus other quadrants), number of positive axillary nodes (1-3 versus 4-9 versus at least 10), and neoadjuvant chemotherapy (yes versus no).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomly assigned 1:1 to postmastectomy radiotherapy with or without internal mammary node irradiation. CT-based 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiotherapy, or volumetric modulated arc therapy may be used. Prescribed dose is 50 Gy in 25 fractions or 43.5 Gy in 15 fractions.

arms.label: IMNI
arms.text: Postmastectomy radiotherapy including internal mammary node irradiation.

arms.label: No IMNI
arms.text: Postmastectomy radiotherapy without internal mammary node irradiation.

NCT04320979.schema_source: Open-access protocol (PMID 34742270) states the 1:1 internal mammary node randomization, stratification factors, and prescribed doses.

arms.label: IT methotrexate

arms.label: Triple intrathecal therapy
arms.text: Triple intrathecal therapy (n=1009).

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SHORTER is a phase 2 trial of salvage MRI-guided radiotherapy. A total of 136 patients are planned, randomized 1:1 with permuted blocks, testing non-inferior 2-year gastrointestinal and genitourinary toxicity.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Stratification is by baseline EPIC bowel and urinary domain scores, nodal treatment, and androgen deprivation therapy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Androgen deprivation therapy and whether to cover nodes are per investigator discretion. Nodal doses, if used, are 25.5 Gy over 2 weeks or 42 Gy over 4 weeks.

arms.label: 5 fractions
arms.text: 32.5 Gy in 5 fractions over 2 weeks.

arms.label: 20 fractions
arms.text: 55 Gy in 20 fractions over 4 weeks.

NCT04422132.schema_source: Open-access protocol (PMID 37608258) states the 5-fraction versus 20-fraction salvage doses, nodal doses, and stratification factors.

schema.label: Entry

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomized 1:2 to placebo or curcumin and received the same preoperative chemoradiation, then surgery.

arms.label: Curcumin
arms.text: Curcumin 4 g orally twice daily throughout chemoradiation and for 6 weeks afterward. Chemoradiation was 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions with capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Stratified randomization in a 2:3 ratio, block size five. The open abstract does not list the stratification factors. All patients received 70 Gy to gross tumour and 50 Gy to areas at risk for subclinical disease with standard fractionation.

arms.label: Panitumumab plus chemoradiotherapy

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Single-centre phase 3. Age older than 3 years, KPS at least 70, able to undergo MRI, and complete resection of one to three brain metastases with cavity maximum diameter at most 4 cm.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Stratified by histology (melanoma versus other), metastasis size (maximum diameter at least 3 cm versus less than 3 cm), and number of metastases (one versus two or three). Block size four.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to cavity radiosurgery within 30 days of surgery or to observation.

arms.label: SRS
arms.text: Single-fraction Gamma Knife radiosurgery to the resection cavity with a 1 mm margin. Prescription doses were 16, 14, and 12 Gy for target volumes of at most 10 cc, 10.1 to 15 cc, and greater than 15 cc.

arms.label: Observation
arms.text: Observation after resection.

NCT00950001.schema_source: Open-access phase 3 report (PMID 28687375) states stratification, assignment to cavity radiosurgery or observation, and the cavity-volume doses.

schema.label: Entry

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomized to conventionally fractionated or hypofractionated whole-breast irradiation, each with a boost.

arms.label: Conventional

schema.text: Patients were randomized 1:1. Chemoradiotherapy was identical. Pembrolizumab 200 mg was given intravenously every 3 weeks for three doses, with no maintenance.
